title: Six annotators over the corroborated components
subtitle: 245 categories from six annotators -- Opus and Fable at three effort levels each -- over 220 corroborated components from 95 sentences. A leaf is a component, coloured by the domain it came from; a hub is one annotator's category, coloured by which annotator named it. Joining two categories from different annotators that share at least 3 components gives 53 clusters, 12 of them carrying all six, covering 211 of the 220 components. Unclustered categories are drawn attached but weak, because a corpus with unplaceable categories should not look tidier than it is.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Lateral churn inside the explicit register
nodes.label: Lateral churn inside the explicit register
nodes.statement: Both sides name sexual anatomy in the same blunt or euphemistic register; what differs is which of the available words comes up and in what order. Nothing leaves the register, changes referent, or changes site.
nodes.spans: One subject area: explicit anatomical description (stroking, the body seen after a massage, oral contact, a sent photo).
nodes.why: These are the entries where the two sides are interchangeable inventories of the same taboo field - cock/dick/shaft against penis/member/bulge - so the only movement is re-ranking. They are kept apart from entries where the explicit word is replaced by a non-explicit one, which is a change of kind, not of order.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Lateral churn inside the violent register
nodes.label: Lateral churn inside the violent register
nodes.statement: Both sides name physical violence on a person; the particular verbs are swapped or re-ranked (beating for choking, hitting for threatening) without the violence being softened, redescribed or displaced anywhere else.
nodes.spans: One subject area: assault (a police officer pinning a woman, a man blocking a door).
nodes.why: The same argument as the explicit churn group, applied to force: no category is crossed, so the movement is re-ranking within one field rather than any displacement out of it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The charged site moves to an uncharged one on the same body
nodes.label: The charged site moves to an uncharged one on the same body
nodes.statement: The act and the body stay put, but the part of the body it lands on shifts from a sexual site to a neighbouring, uncharged one - genitals to fingers, chin, ear, wrist, arm, cheek, or to mild surfaces such as skin and shoulder.
nodes.spans: One subject area: bodily contact prompts (stroking, pinching, mouth to, tongue around, after the massage).
nodes.why: One movement - site displacement with the verb and the participants held constant - as against the group where the whole body drops out of view, and as against the group where the register is merely reshuffled. The distinguishing feature is that a nearby anatomical target replaces the charged one.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Bare anatomy gives way to face, affect and posture
nodes.label: Bare anatomy gives way to face, affect and posture
nodes.statement: What is seen or shown of a person stops being genitals or nakedness and becomes the face, the expression, the emotional state, the posture, or what the person is wearing and doing.
nodes.spans: One subject area: looking at or being sent an image of a body (after the massage, in the video she sent).
nodes.why: Unlike the adjacent-site group the target is no longer an anatomical part at all: the sexual object is replaced by the person as an expressive, clothed, posed subject. That is a single movement from body-as-object to person-as-presence.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The explicit slot empties into words about words
nodes.label: The explicit slot empties into words about words
nodes.statement: Where an anatomical noun is expected, the continuation supplies metalinguistic or purely syntactic material instead - name, word, words, blanks, conjunctions and prepositions - so the sentence exits the topic rather than completing it.
nodes.spans: One subject area: oral contact prompts.
nodes.why: These share a specific exit route that the other explicit groups do not use: not a softer body part, not a neutral scene, but a retreat into talking about naming. All four show name/words/function words taking the noun slot.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Blank tokens in place of a word
nodes.label: Blank tokens in place of a word
nodes.statement: One side supplies ordinary vocabulary while the other supplies literal blanks - runs of underscores, fill-in-the-gap marks, exam scaffolding - so the slot is marked as unfillable rather than filled.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a huge ___, a custodial search, a workplace warning, a hospital complaint, a body after a massage, a crime-scene floor, a shouted insult, a fit of fury.
nodes.why: The same artefact wherever it appears, and independent of what the sentence was about: the contrast is between words and a refusal to produce one. Grouping them by subject would scatter a phenomenon that is plainly one thing.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The slot fills with material that cannot complete it
nodes.label: The slot fills with material that cannot complete it
nodes.statement: One side supplies a word that fits the frame; the other supplies material that does not - subword debris, bare function words, a modifier with no head noun, or a noun the verb cannot take.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: unzipping, feeding, kicking, neighbours, a fairy-tale opening, sitting in a park.
nodes.why: Distinct from the blank group, where the non-word is an explicit placeholder, and distinct from hedging, where the filler is grammatical and meaningful. Here the continuation is formally present but fails to name anything the sentence can use.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Committal content against unspecific filler
nodes.label: Committal content against unspecific filler
nodes.statement: One side names something specific and committal - an act to perform, a dated deadline - while the other fills the slot with modals, auxiliaries, light verbs and open-ended deferral that commit to nothing.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a withheld deposit, a restraint by orderlies, a council officer's verdict, a postponed committee vote.
nodes.why: One movement - loss or gain of specificity in favour of grammatical padding - regardless of whether the padding is a modal (should, could, must), a light verb (had, took, got), or a vague temporal phrase (further, later, next).

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Doing against remarking on it
nodes.label: Doing against remarking on it
nodes.statement: One side supplies the act itself - pay, sue, file, get, say plainly - and the other supplies verbs of commentary and qualification: mention, add, note, clarify, point out, refer, be supposed to.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: advice after an institutional refusal, and describing what someone was doing in a video.
nodes.why: The shared movement is a step back from the action into talk about the action. It is not the same as the recourse group, where the other side names a real channel to act through; here the other side only frames, hedges and annotates.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Immediate response gives way to a named formal channel
nodes.label: Immediate response gives way to a named formal channel
nodes.statement: An unmediated personal reaction - fleeing, quitting, suing on the spot, screaming, or a bare all-purpose verb - stands against the named procedure for registering the same grievance: appeal, file, report, contact, consult, dispute, resign.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a refused asylum claim, a withheld deposit and a disputed repair bill, a workplace warning and a shaved timesheet, a dismissal without severance, a refused insurance claim, a refused maternity request, a child expelled without a hearing.
nodes.why: This is the one movement that recurs most widely across subjects: whatever the grievance, one side acts on it directly and bodily, the other routes it through an institution that has a name for the step. It is kept apart from the group where an institution acts on its own behalf, and from the hedging group where nothing is channelled at all.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Light verbs give way to the institution's named actions
nodes.label: Light verbs give way to the institution's named actions
nodes.statement: An organisation's response moves between all-purpose verbs - send, give, take, do, tell - and the specific acts an institution is able to perform: review, grant, extend, expedite, apologise, investigate, settle, transfer.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a hospital complaint and a repeated visa application.
nodes.why: Here the actor is the institution rather than the claimant, and the contrast is generic-versus-named rather than direct-versus-channelled; the recourse group would blur that distinction.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Handling gives way to an explicit verdict
nodes.label: Handling gives way to an explicit verdict
nodes.statement: Administrative verbs that merely process a case - send, issue, interview, investigate - stand against verbs that pronounce on it: refuse, deny, reject, decline, revoke, grant.
nodes.spans: One subject area: a repeated visa application.
nodes.why: Both entries share the same A side as the deliberative-procedure pair on the same prompt, and differ from it by supplying a decision rather than a process; that is the movement being named, not the subject.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Direct action gives way to the formal instrument
nodes.label: Direct action gives way to the formal instrument
nodes.statement: A decisive or physical act that would settle the matter - evicting, throwing out, firing, suing - stands against the paperwork and process that would accomplish the same end: serving, issuing, filing, escalating, investigating, initiating.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a landlord's response to arrears and to a disputed bill, and a human-resources response to a harassment complaint.
nodes.why: The actor already holds the power in every case, so this is not recourse; the movement is between exercising that power bodily and exercising it through an instrument.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Penalty against accommodation
nodes.label: Penalty against accommodation
nodes.statement: The same decision falls either on the side of extracting and punishing - charge, deduct, cut, evict, terminate - or on the side of relieving: waive, refund, compensate, extend, reduce, offer.
nodes.spans: One subject area: a landlord facing late rent.
nodes.why: Both entries put punitive and remedial dispositions on opposite sides of the same choice; the movement is one of disposition towards the other party, not of formality or of process.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Aggression changes channel: the blow becomes a shout
nodes.label: Aggression changes channel: the blow becomes a shout
nodes.statement: Hostility is held constant while the medium through which it is discharged changes - striking, killing, choking and smashing on one side; screaming, yelling, cursing, threatening, jeering and taunting on the other.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: police restraint, a psychiatric ward, a prison circle, a man blocking a door, a furious phone call to a son, a raised fist, wanting to act in fury, smashed ritual vessels.
nodes.why: In every member the anger survives the transformation and only its outlet moves, which is what separates this from the group where coercion disappears into friendly talk. Mockery and jeering are included because they are aggression delivered vocally, not aggression abandoned.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Coercion dissolves into sociable talk and ordinary activity
nodes.label: Coercion dissolves into sociable talk and ordinary activity
nodes.statement: Violence, stripping, searching and interrogation on one side; on the other, people talking, chatting, arguing companionably, praying, singing, dancing, eating, unpacking and working. The hostility is not rerouted, it is gone.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: strangers entering a room, framed by several different national and ethnic descriptions, and a circle of inmates.
nodes.why: Separated from the channel-change group by what survives: here the other side is not angrier speech but companionable conduct, so the affect itself is what differs. The many ethnic framings are one subject area wearing different labels, not many.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Handling gives way to speaking
nodes.label: Handling gives way to speaking
nodes.statement: A non-violent physical act on an object or a person is replaced by a verbal and social one - telling, calling, inviting, explaining, showing, discussing - so the scene turns from manipulation to address.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a temple offering, a living room, a manager's office, a roommate guided to the floor.
nodes.why: The same act-to-speech move as the aggression group but with no aggression on either side, which matters: what these show is the plain physical act giving up the slot to speech, not anger finding a different outlet.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The act restated as authorised procedure
nodes.label: The act restated as authorised procedure
nodes.statement: The same hands-on treatment of a body appears once as raw or improvised force and once in the vocabulary of trained, warranted procedure: handcuffing, frisking, restraining, sedating, administering, assessing, positioning, instructing.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a police arrest, psychiatric orderlies, strangers in a room, a couch, a roommate on the floor, a driver pulled from a crashed car.
nodes.why: The force is not reduced and not redirected - the hands stay on the body - but it acquires a warrant. That distinguishes it both from violence becoming speech and from violence becoming tenderness, and it recurs across policing, medicine and rescue.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Force gives way to intimate contact
nodes.label: Force gives way to intimate contact
nodes.statement: A scene of bodily contact is rendered either as assault - beating, raping, choking, pinning - or as intimacy: kissing, touching, undressing, stroking, whispering, holding gently. The contact persists, the violence does not.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: partners on a couch, a roommate guided to the floor, a police officer pinning a woman, a man blocking a door.
nodes.why: One movement along a single axis - the same body, the same proximity, recoded from harm to caress or seduction - regardless of whether the intimate side reads as tender or as sexual coercion, which several readers named interchangeably on the same entries.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Heat against composure
nodes.label: Heat against composure
nodes.statement: The same encounter is delivered either hot - yelling, berating, demanding, crying - or composed: calm explanation, apology, polite and measured presentation, smiling.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: a confrontation in a manager's office, a furious phone call, a video sent to someone.
nodes.why: Both sides are the same speech act or the same self-presentation; what moves is the emotional temperature, not the channel and not the content.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The characterisation flips sign
nodes.label: The characterisation flips sign
nodes.statement: The same person or group is characterised with hostile words on one side and warm or admiring words on the other, with the evaluative frame itself unchanged - only its polarity.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a name shouted after someone in the street, and how new neighbours are described.
nodes.why: A sign flip is a different movement from a softening: here the abuse is not made milder or more abstract, it is replaced by praise, or praise by suspicion. The two subject areas show the same flip, which is why they belong together.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Judgment gives way to plain activity
nodes.label: Judgment gives way to plain activity
nodes.statement: Evaluative adjectives about what people are like - rude, loud, friendly, polite - stand against participles naming only what they are doing: talking, working, playing, asking, watching.
nodes.spans: One subject area: describing new neighbours.
nodes.why: Unlike the polarity flip, neither side here is the opposite of the other in value; the move is out of evaluation altogether into neutral description, and it happens from both the hostile and the complimentary starting point.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Obscene slur gives way to moral epithet
nodes.label: Obscene slur gives way to moral epithet
nodes.statement: The insult remains an insult but moves between sexual and scatological slurs and abstract character words - liar, coward, fraud, disgrace, traitor, fool.
nodes.spans: One subject area: a name shouted after someone in the street.
nodes.why: Abuse survives on both sides, so this is not the sign flip; what changes is the kind of badness attributed - bodily and sexual against moral and characterological.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The object is swapped for a harmless one, the frame untouched
nodes.label: The object is swapped for a harmless one, the frame untouched
nodes.statement: The verb and construction are held constant while the thing acted on, found, shown or destroyed changes from something charged - a weapon, genitals, blood, people to kill, pornography, a child - to something ordinary: a wallet, a room, crumbs, pests, cat videos, a pet.
nodes.spans: Many subject areas: a custodial search, late-night viewing, a sent photo, kicking, incitement to kill, a photographed kitchen floor, marks on an arm, entering her ___, feeding.
nodes.why: In every member the sentence keeps its shape and only its object is defused, which is a different operation from softening the verb, redescribing the act, or exiting the topic. Its recurrence across nine unrelated prompts is what makes it one transformation rather than nine coincidences.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Intimate garment gives way to outerwear or a bag
nodes.label: Intimate garment gives way to outerwear or a bag
nodes.statement: What is unzipped shifts from clothing worn close to the body - trousers, skirt, fly, underwear - to an outer layer or a carried container: jacket, hoodie, rucksack, suitcase, purse.
nodes.spans: One subject area: unzipping someone's clothing.
nodes.why: Both entries preserve the act of unzipping and move only the thing unzipped one step away from the skin, which is a narrower and more specific movement than the general defusing of an object.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The weapon changes class
nodes.label: The weapon changes class
nodes.statement: The implement named stays a weapon or a source of injury but changes kind - firearm against blade or blow, specific make against generic category.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a custodial search, and explaining marks on an arm to a nurse.
nodes.why: Neither side defuses the object, so this is not the harmless-swap group; the movement is within the class of dangerous implements.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] All-purpose word against the domain's own word
nodes.label: All-purpose word against the domain's own word
nodes.statement: One side uses generic verbs and superordinate nouns - make, take, put, help, run, salt and pepper - while the other uses the specialised term the domain supplies: maintain, guard, anoint, weave, deface, evacuate, seasoning.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: custody of and ritual with a Torah ark, a craft scene, cooking a soup, desecration of scripture, a house on fire.
nodes.why: One movement of lexical precision, running in both directions across quite different domains; what unites them is that the marked side is the technical or proper term for the same event, not a different event.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The verb slot fills with an inventory of objects
nodes.label: The verb slot fills with an inventory of objects
nodes.statement: Where a continuation verb is expected, the slot is taken instead by nouns naming the furniture and vessels of the scene - chairs, table, armchair, cups, plates, censers, platters.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a living room, and offering bowls in a temple.
nodes.why: All three replace the narration of an action with an enumeration of props, which is a syntactic as well as a semantic move and is not shared by the other specificity groups.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Bare continuation against specified manner
nodes.label: Bare continuation against specified manner
nodes.statement: One side keeps the narration going with pronouns, articles and all-purpose verbs; the other names a particular manner, agent or consequence - settling, curling, striding, sighing, flooding, the police, punching, addressing.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: lighting a fire, stepping out of a car, groceries on a table, a cut brake line, a pistol drawn, a stairwell, a shaved timesheet.
nodes.why: The semantic field of the specified side varies from member to member - rest, violence, speech, rescue - which is exactly why the shared movement cannot be that field; what recurs is the presence or absence of specification itself.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The act stops short of completion
nodes.label: The act stops short of completion
nodes.statement: One side carries the act through - firing, shooting, punching, slamming - while the other halts at its threshold: aiming, cocking, levelling, checking, bracing, clenching, tightening.
nodes.spans: One subject area, in three settings: a drawn pistol, a loaded handgun, a clenched fist.
nodes.why: All three hold the same act in suspension rather than substituting another act for it, which distinguishes them from violence becoming speech, procedure or tenderness.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Handling gives way to checking
nodes.label: Handling gives way to checking
nodes.statement: Verbs of moving things about - taking, pulling, passing, wiping, cleaning - stand against verbs of inspection and verification: checking, inspecting, examining, counting, securing, tightening.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a wallet taken from a jacket, and work on a motorcycle brake line.
nodes.why: In both, the hands do the same work but the purpose shifts from transfer to scrutiny; neither side is more violent or more formal than the other, so the other procedure groups do not fit.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Destruction against restoration
nodes.label: Destruction against restoration
nodes.statement: The same materials are either damaged, burned and thrown away or repaired, replaced, refilled and put back together.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: pages torn from a Quran, and a punctured brake line.
nodes.why: The movement is between breaking and mending on one object, which no other group covers; the subjects are unrelated, so what they share can only be the operation.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Acting on the text gives way to discourse about it
nodes.label: Acting on the text gives way to discourse about it
nodes.statement: Physical handling of a sacred book - tearing, burning, writing, reciting aloud - gives way to talk that takes the text as its object: explaining, discussing, believing, citing other scripture and verses.
nodes.spans: One subject area: pages of a Quran.
nodes.why: Both move from something done to the book to something said about it, which is narrower than the general act-to-speech movement because the speech has the text itself as its content.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Sociable talk against disputation
nodes.label: Sociable talk against disputation
nodes.statement: Companionable or ritual activity - chatting, praying, singing, dancing - stands against argument: bickering, quarrelling, debating, disputing.
nodes.spans: One subject area: strangers entering a room.
nodes.why: Both sides here are verbal and neither is violent, so this is not coercion dissolving into talk; the movement is within talk, from harmony to conflict.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] The field collapses onto its default
nodes.label: The field collapses onto its default
nodes.statement: A spread of plausible alternatives on one side; on the other the stereotyped, expected option that the frame most strongly invites - reading the book, the bench, the catching hand, the roadside ditch, the formula.
nodes.spans: Several subject areas: sitting in a park, opening a book, a tossed bat, a car leaving the road, a workplace warning.
nodes.why: Each member trades breadth for the single canonical completion, which is a movement of distribution shape rather than of register, politeness or topic.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] A person appears where a thing stood
nodes.label: A person appears where a thing stood
nodes.statement: An impersonal continuation - a determiner, an object, a body part - gives way to a human recipient or addressee: him, them, a sister, a friend, a waiting partner, goodbye.
nodes.spans: Three subject areas: a raised hand waving, a stairwell encounter, a bat tossed to someone.
nodes.why: All four put a person into a slot that the other side fills with a thing or a part, so the movement is the animacy of the referent, not politeness or specificity.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Entering a place against entering a life
nodes.label: Entering a place against entering a life
nodes.statement: The same frame takes either a physical location or a person's interior and social sphere - mind, heart, life, family, name - so the verb reads literally on one side and figuratively on the other.
nodes.spans: One subject area: 'He entered her ___'.
nodes.why: These three sit on one axis between the literal room and the metaphorical interior, running in both directions; the entry on the same prompt that swaps anatomy for a room belongs instead with the defused-object group, because there the move is out of the body, not into abstraction.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Same word, different spelling or segmentation
nodes.label: Same word, different spelling or segmentation
nodes.statement: The two sides carry the same lexical content and differ in form alone - British against American spelling, whole contractions against their split stems.
nodes.spans: Two subject areas: a hospital complaint, and a council officer's verdict about mould.
nodes.why: This is an orthographic and tokenisation difference rather than a semantic one, and it is the only movement in the set that leaves meaning entirely untouched.

nodes.id: CAT[opus high] Rank shuffle with no change of kind
nodes.label: Rank shuffle with no change of kind
nodes.statement: Both sides draw on a single unmarked field and differ only in ordering and at the margins of membership; no category is crossed, nothing is softened, nothing is displaced.
nodes.spans: Many subject areas: a workplace warning, a huge ___, a furious phone call, feeding animals, a carried body, a photographed floor, an opened letter, entering her ___, stroking a beard.
nodes.why: The shared movement is the null one, and it is worth holding together because what it shows - that a slot can be reweighted without any transformation of kind - is the same observation wherever it appears. It is kept apart from the explicit and violent churn groups only because there a marked register is being held constant, which is itself the thing observed.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Physical force gives way to verbal action
nodes.label: Physical force gives way to verbal action
nodes.statement: On one side the continuation is a bodily act done to someone (beating, stripping, dragging, restraining); on the other the same slot is filled by talking, arguing, explaining or discussing. The scene keeps its participants and loses its physical contact, which is carried instead by speech.
nodes.spans: Several: strangers entering a room (many nationalities), a prison landing, a psychiatric ward, a doorway confrontation, a phone call to a son, a couch scene.
nodes.why: The variable across these entries is only who is in the room; the movement is identical in every one - an act of force in the continuation slot is exchanged for an act of speech. Grouping them is what separates that movement from the ethnic or institutional subject matter that differs between them.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Blow becomes outcry
nodes.label: Blow becomes outcry
nodes.statement: A physical blow or lethal impulse on one side, a vocal discharge on the other - screaming, shouting, roaring, jeering, taunting. The aggression is not withdrawn but routed through the voice.
nodes.spans: Several: a raised or clenched fist, a furious wish, smashed ritual vessels, an arrest on the ground, a prison circle.
nodes.why: Distinguished from the group above by what the speech is: not conversation but noise made in anger. Every member keeps the anger and changes only its channel, so the two sides are the same affect in two media.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Handling a thing gives way to addressing people
nodes.label: Handling a thing gives way to addressing people
nodes.statement: One side manipulates objects or a body - placing, pouring, pulling, leading; the other turns outward into speech and sociability, telling, inviting, chatting, explaining. The act stops being done to something and starts being done to someone in words.
nodes.spans: Several: a manager's office, a temple offering, a roommate on the floor, cushions in a living room, a stairwell.
nodes.why: The A sides here are ordinary handling, not violence, so the transformation cannot be read as harm being withdrawn; what recurs is the exchange of manual action for verbal address, which is a different claim from the violence-to-talk groups.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The same act renamed as sanctioned procedure
nodes.label: The same act renamed as sanctioned procedure
nodes.statement: Force applied to a person is re-described in institutional or clinical vocabulary - handcuff, frisk, restrain, subdue, administer, examine, position, apply. The hands keep doing something to the body; what changes is that the vocabulary is now the vocabulary of a trained role.
nodes.spans: Several: police restraint, a psychiatric ward, a crash scene, a roommate on the floor, a couch.
nodes.why: These are not softenings - the B sides are still physical and often still coercive. What unites them is the register of the naming, and that is a single move visible in policing, medicine and first response alike.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The act arrested before discharge
nodes.label: The act arrested before discharge
nodes.statement: One side completes the act - fires, strikes, does; the other stops short in preparation, verification or containment - aiming, cocking, checking, inspecting, securing, holding the fist closed. The energy is present in both and expended in only one.
nodes.spans: Several: a clenched fist, a pistol drawn, a handgun on a table, a motorcycle brake line.
nodes.why: The same structure appears on a body, on a weapon and on a machine: the decisive moment is replaced by the careful handling that would precede it, which is a movement about completion and not about violence.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Destruction answered by repair
nodes.label: Destruction answered by repair
nodes.statement: One side damages or discards the object; the other restores, replaces, refits or reassembles it. The same object is at stake and the hands move in opposite directions on it.
nodes.spans: Two: a desecrated Quran and a cut brake line.
nodes.why: Both entries turn on the reversal of a damaging act into a restorative one on the identical object, which is narrower and more specific than a general softening.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Damage named more specifically
nodes.label: Damage named more specifically
nodes.statement: Generic verbs of breaking - broke, damaged, destroyed, tore - on one side; on the other the particular means and marks of the defacement, spray-painted, scrawled, smeared, shredded, flushed.
nodes.spans: One: desecration of a religious object (a Quran, a Torah ark).
nodes.why: The severity does not change between the sides; only the resolution of the description does, which separates these from the softening groups they sit beside.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Verbs give way to an inventory of objects
nodes.label: Verbs give way to an inventory of objects
nodes.statement: One side continues with what was done; the other continues by naming more of the furniture of the scene - vessels, plates, censers, chairs, armchairs, ottomans. The clause turns from action into enumeration.
nodes.spans: Two: a temple offering and a living room.
nodes.why: This is a change of grammatical direction rather than of content - the slot stops taking a verb and starts taking a noun - and it shows up in a sacred setting and a domestic one alike.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Sexual anatomy exchanged for a neutral site on the same body
nodes.label: Sexual anatomy exchanged for a neutral site on the same body
nodes.statement: One side names genitals or breasts; the other names a part of the same body that carries no charge - hand, finger, thumb, wrist, ear, earlobe, cheek, chin, shoulder, neck. The gesture, the toucher and the touched all persist; only the landing site moves outward from the centre.
nodes.spans: One: explicit sexual contact (stroking, pinching, mouth and tongue prompts).
nodes.why: These share not just a subject but a precise structure - a minimal displacement along the body rather than a change of scene, register or topic - which is what separates them from the euphemism and topic-flight groups drawn from the very same prompts.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Explicit term exchanged for an indirect one in the same register
nodes.label: Explicit term exchanged for an indirect one in the same register
nodes.statement: Both sides stay sexual, but one uses the blunt or clinical name and the other an oblique one - member, length, manhood, bulge, boner, crown, core, engorged - or moves from the genital to the clothed or peripheral sexual body.
nodes.spans: One: explicit sexual description.
nodes.why: Nothing leaves the erotic frame in these; the movement is a choice of name for the same referent, which is a different transformation from abandoning the referent altogether.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The sexual body gives way to the face and its state
nodes.label: The sexual body gives way to the face and its state
nodes.statement: One side itemises the body sexually; the other looks at the face, the eyes, the expression, or at the body's condition and repose - asleep, peaceful, flushed, exhausted, worried. The gaze stays on the person and stops being a gaze at parts.
nodes.spans: One: a body seen after a massage, in both directions of gender.
nodes.why: The replacement is consistently a sign of the person's inner state rather than another body part or another word for the same part, which distinguishes it both from the adjacent-site group and from the euphemism group.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Undress described as posture and activity
nodes.label: Undress described as posture and activity
nodes.statement: One side gives the state of the body - naked, topless, dressed, breasts; the other gives what the body is doing - sitting, standing, walking, dancing, holding, sleeping. A description of exposure becomes a description of conduct.
nodes.spans: One: a woman seen in a video or after a massage.
nodes.why: Both turn a static anatomical predicate into a verb of ordinary activity, which is a narrower move than the general retreat from explicit vocabulary.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The taboo subject replaced by an unremarkable one
nodes.label: The taboo subject replaced by an unremarkable one
nodes.statement: One side is explicitly sexual; the other belongs to a different and innocuous world altogether - pets, children, television, rooms of a house. Not a softer word for the same thing but a different thing in its place.
nodes.spans: Several: private viewing, a photo sent, a body entered.
nodes.why: Unlike the adjacent-site and euphemism groups, nothing of the original referent survives here; the whole domain is swapped, and the same wholesale swap appears with media, photographs and architecture.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The clause leaves its content for grammar or noise
nodes.label: The clause leaves its content for grammar or noise
nodes.statement: One side holds a coherent semantic field; the other empties into function words, metalinguistic tokens like name and words, discourse filler, or sub-lexical fragments. The sentence keeps going and stops meaning anything in particular.
nodes.spans: Several: explicit contact, a kick, feeding animals, an unzipping, neighbours being described.
nodes.why: The shared movement is the loss of the content slot itself rather than any substitution within it, and it is visible on transgressive and wholly neutral prompts alike - which is why the explicit members belong here and not with the sexual-vocabulary groups.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Blank placeholders against real words
nodes.label: Blank placeholders against real words
nodes.statement: One side of the pair is filled with underscore runs or bare template scaffolding; the other with ordinary lexical continuations. The slot is either refused or filled.
nodes.spans: Several: a prison search, a huge something, a street insult, a furious wish, a written warning, a hospital complaint, a body after a massage, a crime-scene floor.
nodes.why: This is the clearest cross-subject transformation in the set: the same non-answer appears on transgressive and innocuous prompts, so it is a property of the slot being filled, not of what would fill it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Reordering within one register
nodes.label: Reordering within one register
nodes.statement: Both sides draw on the same vocabulary at the same level of decorum and specificity; what differs is which members sit at the top. Nothing is added, withdrawn or renamed - the ranking is simply reshuffled.
nodes.spans: Several: a scolding phone call, rooms entered, a huge something, a wallet, explicit stroking, a written warning, feeding animals, an opened letter, a body carried out.
nodes.why: The absence of a directional change is itself the shared transformation, and it recurs across explicit, bureaucratic and wholly neutral prompts - so it is a property of the comparison, not of any one vocabulary. Merging these with the groups that do have a direction would falsely attribute a movement to entries that show none.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] A spread field collapses onto the default
nodes.label: A spread field collapses onto the default
nodes.statement: One side offers a wide scatter of admissible continuations; the other narrows onto the one or two that the frame most expects - read after opening a book, grass and bench in a park, a fixed opening formula.
nodes.spans: Several: a book opened, a park bench, a written warning, a fairy-tale opening.
nodes.why: The movement is about the shape of the distribution rather than its content: variety on one side, the conventional answer on the other, in four unrelated frames.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The characterization flips its sign
nodes.label: The characterization flips its sign
nodes.statement: The same slot carries a hostile or degrading description on one side and a warm, admiring or contented one on the other - slur against compliment, suspicious and fighting against friendly and courteous, crying against smiling.
nodes.spans: Several: an epithet shouted in the street, new neighbours of several nationalities, a woman in a video.
nodes.why: In each the referent is unchanged and only its valence reverses; this is a polarity flip rather than a softening, which is what separates it from the group where a slur becomes a milder insult but stays an insult.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Evaluation traded for ongoing activity
nodes.label: Evaluation traded for ongoing activity
nodes.statement: One side judges the people - rude, loud, friendly, polite, cordial; the other just reports what they are doing - talking, playing, working, watching, busy. A verdict on character is exchanged for an unevaluated description of behaviour.
nodes.spans: One: neighbours described in a fixed frame.
nodes.why: This is not the polarity flip: it holds whether the judgement being dropped is praise or complaint, so what moves is the presence of evaluation itself, not its sign.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Taboo epithet becomes a mild insult
nodes.label: Taboo epithet becomes a mild insult
nodes.statement: One side uses sexual or profane abuse - whore, slut, cunt, fucking, bastard; the other keeps the abuse but drains the taboo out of it - liar, coward, fool, fraud, disgrace. The speaker is insulting on both sides.
nodes.spans: One: an epithet shouted down the street, at a woman and at a man.
nodes.why: Grouped apart from the polarity flip because the target is still being denigrated; the movement is the loss of the sexual or profane charge, not of the hostility.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The human participant becomes an animal or an object
nodes.label: The human participant becomes an animal or an object
nodes.statement: One side puts a person in the slot - kids, babies, men, a woman, a boy; the other puts a creature, a pest or a thing - bugs, vermin, weeds, a pebble, a football, birds, trolls. The act persists and its human counterpart disappears.
nodes.spans: Several: an incitement to kill, a kick, the feeding of dependents.
nodes.why: The same de-personing shows up under violence and under care, which is the evidence that it is a move on the participant slot rather than a property of aggressive verbs.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Heat exchanged for composure
nodes.label: Heat exchanged for composure
nodes.statement: One side is heated delivery - yelling, berating, screaming, demanding, begging; the other is measured address of the same complaint - calmly, politely, explaining, reasoning, presenting, listening. The grievance survives, the temperature does not.
nodes.spans: Two: a workplace confrontation and a phone call to a son.
nodes.why: Both keep the speaker, the addressee and the complaint, and change only the manner of speaking, which is a narrower move than the shift from action into speech.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Direct action replaced by a formal instrument
nodes.label: Direct action replaced by a formal instrument
nodes.statement: A party with power over another acts on them directly on one side - evicting, throwing out, selling, kicking, firing, suing - and on the other reaches for the instrument that would do the same thing formally - serving, issuing, filing, withholding, terminating, repossessing, opening an investigation.
nodes.spans: Two: landlord and tenant, and an employer's HR department.
nodes.why: The interest of the party is identical on both sides; only the route changes, from the hand to the document. That is one move, and it is the mirror of the aggrieved party's move in the next group.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The grievance routed into a named channel
nodes.label: The grievance routed into a named channel
nodes.statement: One side answers a wrong with whatever comes first - generic modals, an outburst, or a threat to sue - while the other names an institutional step: contact, file, report, consult, appeal, document, escalate. The complaint is unchanged and acquires an address.
nodes.spans: Several: dismissal without severance, a refused insurance claim, a withheld deposit, maternity leave, an expulsion, shaved timesheet hours.
nodes.why: The A sides differ in kind - anger, litigation, nothing much - and the B sides converge on the same small vocabulary of official first steps, which shows the transformation is the channelling and not any particular starting point.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Leaving the situation against contesting it
nodes.label: Leaving the situation against contesting it
nodes.statement: One side gets out - fled, left, moved, travelled, packed, quit; the other stays and works the mechanism - appealed, applied, lodged, challenged, contested, or asked to speak to someone. Exit and voice occupy the same slot.
nodes.spans: Two: a refused asylum claim or visa, and a written warning at work.
nodes.why: In each the person is the weaker party and the two sides are the two available responses to that position; the recurrence across immigration and employment shows it is the response type moving, not the setting.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Penalty gives way to accommodation
nodes.label: Penalty gives way to accommodation
nodes.statement: One side is the punitive or extractive disposal - charge, deduct, cut, evict, deport, ban; the other is relief or deliberation in the other party's favour - waive, refund, extend, compensate, grant, reconsider, expedite, pause. The institution acts either against or for the person.
nodes.spans: Two: a landlord over late rent, and the Home Office over a visa.
nodes.why: The two prompts are institutionally unrelated, and their B vocabularies converge on the same stance of leniency and deferral, so the movement is the institution's posture rather than the specific remedy.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The decision named as a verdict
nodes.label: The decision named as a verdict
nodes.statement: One side handles the case with unmarked administrative verbs - send, take, give, issue, look, interview; the other pronounces on it - refuse, deny, reject, decline, revoke, grant. The outcome stops being implied by the handling and becomes a word.
nodes.spans: One: a third visa application before the Home Office.
nodes.why: Both entries turn on the appearance of explicit adjudicative vocabulary rather than on how harsh the outcome is - the verdict words on the B sides run in both directions.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Deeds give way to states, modals and thoughts
nodes.label: Deeds give way to states, modals and thoughts
nodes.statement: One side continues with things done - went, took, put, strapped, dragged, fixed; the other with what was or might be - had, was, could, should, must, felt, thought, knew, became. The clause stops recording an act and starts recording a condition or an attitude toward one.
nodes.spans: Two: a council officer blaming a tenant for mould, and orderlies handling a patient.
nodes.why: The same grammatical retreat - from lexical verb to auxiliary, modal or mental predicate - appears where the A side is mundane and where it is coercive, so it is not the violence that is being withdrawn but the eventhood.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The act replaced by commentary on it
nodes.label: The act replaced by commentary on it
nodes.statement: One side does or decides something - get, take, pay, sue, file, find; the other steps outside to talk about it - mention, note, add, clarify, say, point out, emphasize, qualify. The continuation becomes discourse about the situation rather than a move within it.
nodes.spans: Several: first-person advice after a dismissal, an insurance refusal, denied maternity leave, a withheld deposit, and a video being described.
nodes.why: The B vocabularies are a tight and recurring set of metadiscursive verbs, quite distinct from the institutional-channel verbs of the recourse group, even though several members come from the same prompts.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Unmarked general vocabulary against marked specific vocabulary
nodes.label: Unmarked general vocabulary against marked specific vocabulary
nodes.statement: The same event is carried on one side by light, high-frequency words - took, made, gave, went, get, a bare date - and on the other by vocabulary specific to the domain: supervised, guarded, anointed, evacuated, apologised, seasoning, resigned, drummed, until further notice.
nodes.spans: Several: care of a Torah ark, a temple offering, a written warning, a hospital complaint, a cut brake line, a pot of soup, a postponed vote, a house on fire, visitors to a room.
nodes.why: Nothing in these is softened, escalated or displaced; the one thing that changes is lexical resolution, and it changes in the same way across ritual, medical, culinary, bureaucratic and emergency material.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Bare continuation against elaborated manner
nodes.label: Bare continuation against elaborated manner
nodes.statement: One side moves the scene along with unmarked verbs and pronouns - then, went, took, he, she; the other supplies manner, hesitation or inward notice - stride, cross, sighed, decided, proceeded, thought, saw. The same next moment is either passed over or dwelt on.
nodes.spans: Several: a pistol drawn, a woman stepping out of a car, groceries on a table.
nodes.why: Each pairs a skeletal narrative continuation against a textured one at the identical point in the sentence, which is a movement in narration rather than in what is narrated.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Lateral swap within the vocabulary of force
nodes.label: Lateral swap within the vocabulary of force
nodes.statement: Both sides are violent and at the same pitch; what changes is which violence - striking against restraining, choking against dragging, specific blows against generic assault and abuse.
nodes.spans: Two: an arrest on the ground, and a doorway or room confrontation.
nodes.why: No register, target or channel moves in these, so they cannot join the procedure, speech or tenderness groups they resemble at first glance; they record substitution inside a single field.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The alarming referent becomes an ordinary one
nodes.label: The alarming referent becomes an ordinary one
nodes.statement: One side names something dangerous, forensic or bodily - a weapon, a gunshot wound, blood, vomit, a river, human or animal remains; the other names something banal in the same slot - a wallet, a vaccination mark, crumbs and grease, a roadside ditch, dust.
nodes.spans: Several: a prison search, a nurse examining marks on an arm, a car leaving the road, a photographed kitchen floor.
nodes.why: Each holds the frame fixed - the search, the examination, the crash, the photograph - and replaces only the gravity of what is found, which is one transformation appearing in policing, medicine and accident narration.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Firearm against blade or blow
nodes.label: Firearm against blade or blow
nodes.statement: Both sides name a weapon or the injury it makes; the movement is between the gun and the knife, the gunshot and the laceration, or between a named weapon and the generic word for one.
nodes.spans: Two: a prison search and marks on a patient's arm.
nodes.why: Kept apart from the alarming-to-banal group because nothing is defused here - the danger is constant and only its instrument changes class.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] What is unzipped moves off the body
nodes.label: What is unzipped moves off the body
nodes.statement: One side unzips clothing at the body's centre - fly, jeans, trousers, panties, skirt; the other unzips something outer or carried - a jacket, hoodie, bag, backpack, suitcase. The same gesture, a different object and a different distance from the skin.
nodes.spans: One: an unzipping, in both directions of gender.
nodes.why: Both entries turn on the object class of the unzipped thing rather than on its name or its owner, and the container answer appears on both prompts.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Force becomes undressing
nodes.label: Force becomes undressing
nodes.statement: One side is blunt violence - beat, choke, strangle, punch, rape; the other is sexual handling of the clothed body - undress, unbutton, unzip, strip, grope, touch. The coercion persists and changes its object from harm to exposure.
nodes.spans: Two: an arrest on the ground, and a blocked doorway.
nodes.why: These are not softenings into intimacy: the B sides remain non-consensual and simply redirect the hands to clothing, which distinguishes them from the tenderness group.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Force becomes tenderness
nodes.label: Force becomes tenderness
nodes.statement: One side pins, throws, beats or rapes; the other whispers, kisses, holds, wraps, teases, kneels, does something gently. The bodies remain in the same configuration and the contact between them is recoded as care or play.
nodes.spans: One: a person taken down onto a floor or held on a couch.
nodes.why: Grouped by the affective recoding of identical physical contact, which is a different move from redirecting the contact sexually or renaming it procedurally - both of which appear on these very prompts as separate entries.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Entering a place against entering a person
nodes.label: Entering a place against entering a person
nodes.statement: One side of the pair is a physical or architectural interior - house, room, bedroom, office; the other is a psychological one - mind, heart, life, soul, world, dreams. The same verb takes either a place or an inner life.
nodes.spans: One: the frame he entered her.
nodes.why: Both entries move along the concrete-to-figurative axis in the same slot, which is distinct from the room-for-anatomy swap that also occurs on this prompt.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The act on the text gives way to discourse about the text
nodes.label: The act on the text gives way to discourse about the text
nodes.statement: One side does something to the book - tore, burned, threw, wrote, read aloud; the other moves into the tradition around it - hadith, Sunnah, verses, believed, understood, explained, discussed. The handling is replaced by interpretation and citation.
nodes.spans: One: pages of the Quran.
nodes.why: Both exit the physical event into commentary on the scripture rather than into any other action, and they do it from opposite starting points (desecration and reading).

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Action gives way to the actor's own posture
nodes.label: Action gives way to the actor's own posture
nodes.statement: One side keeps doing things to objects or moving through the scene; the other resolves into what the body itself does - kneeling, bowing, sitting, settling, curling, collapsing, coming to rest.
nodes.spans: Two: a temple offering and a fireside.
nodes.why: In both the transitive act is replaced not by another act on the world but by the subject's own disposition in space, which is the same structural retreat in a sacred and a domestic scene.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] A calm act replaced by a forceful one
nodes.label: A calm act replaced by a forceful one
nodes.statement: One side is gentle or neutral handling - settled, laid, leaned, placed, covered, returning, coming; the other is force - kicked, punched, slammed, threw, striking, firing. The same juncture is either uneventful or violent.
nodes.spans: Two: cushions on a couch, and a landlord on a stairwell.
nodes.why: Both introduce violence where the other side has none, which is the inverse of the many entries that withdraw it; the pairing of a domestic and a threatening scene shows it is not the menace in the prompt doing the work.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] An impersonal object slot takes a person
nodes.label: An impersonal object slot takes a person
nodes.statement: One side fills the slot with impersonal material - it, the, a, a clause continuing the action; the other with a person or a person-directed form - him, her, them, us, goodbye, hello. The continuation acquires an addressee.
nodes.spans: Two: a hand raised to wave, and a landlord passing a tenant on a stairwell.
nodes.why: Both turn on whether the slot is filled by a human recipient or by grammatical scaffolding, which is a movement in who the sentence is about rather than in what happens.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] The landing site becomes a prepared recipient
nodes.label: The landing site becomes a prepared recipient
nodes.statement: One side names an arbitrary body part or the ground the object reaches - feet, head, chest, back, side; the other names someone ready to receive it - an outstretched or waiting hand, a glove, a partner, a brother, a friend. The throw acquires a catcher.
nodes.spans: One: a bat tossed toward someone.
nodes.why: All three replace an incidental point of contact with a person or hand held ready, which is a single reorientation of the act toward reception rather than impact.

nodes.id: CAT[opus xhigh] Sociable activity becomes verbal conflict
nodes.label: Sociable activity becomes verbal conflict
nodes.statement: One side has people talking, praying, singing or dancing together; the other has them arguing, quarrelling, bickering or debating. They remain in words and stop being at ease with each other.
nodes.spans: One: visitors entering a room.
nodes.why: Both keep the group in the same verbal mode and move only its temperature, which is why they do not belong with the entries where physical violence turns into talk.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Blank placeholder against named filler
nodes.label: Blank placeholder against named filler
nodes.statement: One condition fills the slot with underscore runs, blank rules and exam-sheet scaffolding, the other with ordinary words; the contrast is between a token that occupies the position without naming anything and a token that names something.
nodes.spans: several: possession search, insult, anger, workplace discipline, hospital complaint, massage scene, forensic photography
nodes.why: The material differs completely across these - a body, an insult, a weapon, a floor - but the movement is identical and has nothing to do with the subject: on one side the position is held open by a typographic blank, on the other it is filled. No member trades one meaning for another meaning.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Orthographic variant split
nodes.label: Orthographic variant split
nodes.statement: The two sides hold the same lexeme in two written forms, differing only in spelling convention or in whether a contraction is kept whole or split at its clitic.
nodes.spans: two: hospital complaint and a tenant narrating a council decision
nodes.why: Both are a division inside the writing system, not the lexicon: apologised against apologized, didn't against didn. Nothing about who acts or what is done changes, which is what separates these from every semantic group.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The slot loses its selectional fit
nodes.label: The slot loses its selectional fit
nodes.statement: One side supplies a filler the frame can actually take, the other supplies function words, sub-lexical fragments or nouns the frame cannot govern, so the sentence stops cohering at that position.
nodes.spans: several: kicking, feeding, undressing
nodes.why: These share a breakdown rather than a substitution. The degraded side is not a softer or harsher way of saying the same thing - it is material that cannot complete the phrase at all, whether it arrives as discourse particles, as byte fragments, or as body parts offered to a verb that needs a garment.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Modifier or pronoun where the head was
nodes.label: Modifier or pronoun where the head was
nodes.statement: One side completes the phrase with the expected content word, the other with a word of a different class - a bare adjective, an object pronoun, a preposition - leaving the phrase unheaded.
nodes.spans: several: a park bench, a stairwell encounter, neighbours being characterised
nodes.why: The grammatical category of the filler is what moves, not its meaning. In each case one condition still supplies the noun or predicate the slot wants and the other supplies its satellite, so the reading has to be completed by the reader.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Reweighting inside a closed class
nodes.label: Reweighting inside a closed class
nodes.statement: Both sides draw from the same closed class of pronouns, determiners and directional particles, with much the same inventory; only the ordering inside that class differs.
nodes.spans: several: a story opening, a letter being opened, a body being carried
nodes.why: No content word enters or leaves on either side. These look like transformations of the scene only if one reads the particles as if they carried the scene; what actually moves is rank order among grammatical words.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Reshuffle inside one unmarked field
nodes.label: Reshuffle inside one unmarked field
nodes.statement: Both sides draw on substantially the same field of ordinary, unmarked vocabulary for the slot, with heavy overlap of members; what differs is which of them leads.
nodes.spans: several: a phone scolding, workplace discipline, a huge something, rooms, grooming, feeding, a forensic floor, a house fire
nodes.why: Grouped on the absence of movement rather than on subject: no register changes, no referent class changes, no act is exchanged for another kind of act. Keeping them together prevents rank noise in eleven different scenes from being read as eleven different findings.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Churn inside the explicit register
nodes.label: Churn inside the explicit register
nodes.statement: Both sides name the same sexual referent in equally explicit terms, trading one taboo or slang word for another - crude for slangy, clinical for coarse - without leaving the register.
nodes.spans: one: explicit sexual anatomy, across several scenes (stroking, a massage, a sent photograph, oral sex)
nodes.why: Held apart from the unmarked reshuffle above because here both sides are marked: the exchange is of one taboo word for another for the very same body, which is a different fact about the two conditions than ordinary rank noise. Held apart from the softening groups because no member leaves the explicit register.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Sexual site displaced to a neutral one
nodes.label: Sexual site displaced to a neutral one
nodes.statement: The slot stays a body part but moves off the sexual zone onto an ordinary one - cheek, arm, wrist, chin, finger, throat - so the act keeps its form and loses its object.
nodes.spans: one: bodily contact, across pinching, stroking, mouth-to-body and oral scenes
nodes.why: One movement in nine scenes: the substitution is anatomical and local, a neighbouring or peripheral site standing in for a genital or erogenous one. It is not topic flight - the body is still there - and not synonym churn, because the replacement is not another name for the same part.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Anatomy replaced by bodily state
nodes.label: Anatomy replaced by bodily state
nodes.statement: A named body part gives way to the condition that body is in - flushed, swollen, puffy, trembling, sweaty, bruised - so a noun for a part becomes a description of a state.
nodes.spans: one: the body in sexual and post-massage scenes
nodes.why: Distinct from displacement to a neighbouring part: nothing else is named instead, the reading turns from where to how. Both members keep sensation and arousal fully in view while removing the part that would have carried them.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The body yields to the face
nodes.label: The body yields to the face
nodes.statement: Explicit anatomy is replaced by the face and what it shows - eyes, smile, expression, asleep, worried - or by the small objects near it, moving attention from the exposed body to legible affect.
nodes.spans: one: what is seen after a massage, in both directions of gaze
nodes.why: The substitute is consistently the site where feeling is read rather than another site of contact, which separates these from the neutral-body-part group: a face is not a peripheral body part, it is the alternative to looking at the body.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The body yields to posture and activity
nodes.label: The body yields to posture and activity
nodes.statement: A named or exposed body part is replaced by what the person is doing or how they are arranged - lying, sitting, standing, walking, dancing, wearing something.
nodes.spans: one: bodies seen in a video and after a massage
nodes.why: Both trade a nominal body for a predicate of comportment. The person stays in frame, fully occupying the slot, but is described by attitude rather than by part, which is neither a face-substitution nor a change of topic.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The viewed object becomes innocuous
nodes.label: The viewed object becomes innocuous
nodes.statement: What is looked at or sent changes class entirely, from explicitly sexual content to ordinary media and household subjects - pets, family, television, a video.
nodes.spans: two: private viewing on a laptop and a photograph sent to someone
nodes.why: In both the whole topic of the image leaves rather than being renamed or displaced onto a nearby body; the slot is occupied by content that belongs to an entirely different activity, which no member of the anatomy groups does.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Explicit noun exits into discourse
nodes.label: Explicit noun exits into discourse
nodes.statement: The explicit body-part slot is taken instead by metalinguistic and function tokens - name, words, word, like, as, and - so the sentence stops referring and starts talking about itself.
nodes.spans: one: oral sex scenes, in both directions
nodes.why: The escape is not to another body part but out of reference altogether. Unlike the collapse group, the tokens are well formed and the sentence reads; what has gone is anything for the verb to act on.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Body becomes place or belonging
nodes.label: Body becomes place or belonging
nodes.statement: A body interior as the object of entering gives way to a room, a house, a name, a vehicle or another possession - the same verb read spatially or socially rather than bodily.
nodes.spans: one: entering a person
nodes.why: Both turn on the double reading of the verb. The movement is a change in what kind of thing is entered, from anatomy to premises and belongings, which is sharper than substituting one body part for another.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Concrete place against abstract interior
nodes.label: Concrete place against abstract interior
nodes.statement: The slot alternates between a physical room or body and an abstract interior - mind, heart, life, soul, world - so a literal entry and a figurative one occupy the same position.
nodes.spans: one: entering a person
nodes.why: These two are the same axis taken in opposite directions, which is why they belong together under a direction-neutral reading: one side is always locatable in space, the other never is.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Worn garment against carried case
nodes.label: Worn garment against carried case
nodes.statement: What is unzipped shifts between clothing worn close to the body and an outer layer or a container that is carried - bag, backpack, suitcase, jacket, hood.
nodes.spans: one: unzipping, in both directions of gender
nodes.why: Same movement twice: the zip stays, its owner changes from the body to luggage or outerwear. The undressing reading survives on one side and is entirely absent on the other.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Force redirected into sexual contact
nodes.label: Force redirected into sexual contact
nodes.statement: A blow or a killing grip is replaced by a sexual handling of the same body - undressing, groping, kissing, unbuttoning - so coercion is retained and its aim is changed.
nodes.spans: two: a police restraint and a blocked doorway
nodes.why: Both sides are assaults; what moves is the kind. This is not a softening, because the substitute is itself violating, and not a lateral swap within violence, because the replacement vocabulary belongs to a different domain of contact.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Force against gentle handling
nodes.label: Force against gentle handling
nodes.statement: The same contact between two bodies is described either as violence - pinning, beating, throwing, forcing - or as tender, playful or careful handling: gently, whispered, kissed, tickled, laid, covered.
nodes.spans: several: a roommate on the floor, a partner on a couch, cushions being held down
nodes.why: One axis of manner running through three scenes: identical physical configurations read as assault on one side and as care or play on the other. The bodies and the positions do not change, only the force applied to them.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The act recoded as clinical procedure
nodes.label: The act recoded as clinical procedure
nodes.statement: A graphic or forceful act is restated in clinical and instructional vocabulary - performed, applied, administered, positioned, instructed, engaged, subjected - so the deed acquires the grammar of a procedure carried out on a patient.
nodes.spans: two: guiding a roommate to the floor and holding a partner down
nodes.why: Both keep the act in place and change the discourse it is reported in. The substitute terms are not softer synonyms but terms from a professional register, which is what distinguishes this from the force-against-gentleness axis.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Lateral swap within violence
nodes.label: Lateral swap within violence
nodes.statement: Both sides are violent, and the exchange is between kinds of force - striking against strangling, restraining against beating, tying against hitting - with no change in register or severity.
nodes.spans: several: a police restraint, a group entering a room, a psychiatric ward, a blocked doorway
nodes.why: Grouped on the absence of any exit from violence: nothing is defused, proceduralised or made verbal. Four scenes that elsewhere produce softening produce here only a redistribution among assault verbs.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Force becomes police procedure
nodes.label: Force becomes police procedure
nodes.statement: Blows given by an officer are replaced by the named steps of custody - handcuff, cuff, frisk, pat, search, question, interrogate, restrain, arrest.
nodes.spans: one: an officer pinning someone to the ground
nodes.why: The substitute vocabulary is specifically the procedural repertoire of the same role, so the violence is not removed but licensed. Kept apart from the general procedure group because the actor and the act are unchanged - only their legality is.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The aftermath handled by trained response
nodes.label: The aftermath handled by trained response
nodes.statement: What follows an injury shifts from bare or violent handling of the body to the trained repertoire of first response and custody - checked, assessed, administered, examined, alerted, questioned, arrested.
nodes.spans: one: a driver being taken from a car, helped in one scene and dragged in the other
nodes.why: Both put competent procedure where narration or violence stood. The movement is about who is treated as being on the scene - bystanders or trained responders - rather than about the severity of what happened.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The act suspended before discharge
nodes.label: The act suspended before discharge
nodes.statement: A completed act - a shot fired, a punch thrown, a shout - is replaced by the preparation that stops short of it: aiming, cocking, levelling, checking, bracing, tightening, gripping.
nodes.spans: two: a drawn pistol and a clenched fist
nodes.why: The three members share a held threshold: the sequence is elaborated right up to the point of release and the release never arrives. This is a different movement from proceduralisation, because nothing institutional replaces the act - it simply does not happen.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Handling against inspection
nodes.label: Handling against inspection
nodes.statement: One side performs or transfers - takes, gives, cleans, refills, hands over - and the other inspects and verifies: checked, counted, examined, inspected, secured, tightened.
nodes.spans: two: a wallet taken from a jacket and a brake line on a motorcycle
nodes.why: The same objects are in the same hands on both sides; what changes is whether the hands are doing or confirming. Two very different subject areas produce the identical split between action and verification.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Assault gives way to conversation
nodes.label: Assault gives way to conversation
nodes.statement: People entering a room, or surrounding someone, either set about them physically - beat, strip, search, interrogate, shoot - or fall into ordinary sociable activity: talk, chat, discuss, converse, sing, pray, unpack.
nodes.spans: two scene types: a group arriving in a room and prisoners surrounding a man; across many named groups
nodes.why: The largest single movement here: the aggressive reading of an arrival is exchanged for a sociable one. Grouped on that exchange and not on who arrives - the named group varies across nearly every member, and the movement is constant, which is exactly what shows the group identity is not doing the work.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The blow becomes a voice
nodes.label: The blow becomes a voice
nodes.statement: Physical violence and vocal discharge stand on opposite sides: striking, killing and beating against shouting, screaming, jeering, taunting, cursing and arguing - the same fury expressed by the hand or by the mouth.
nodes.spans: several: a raised fist, furious wishes, prisoners, orderlies, a blocked doorway, a mother on the telephone
nodes.why: One substitution running through six scenes, and readable in both directions - a mother's plain talk becoming a thrash and a punch becoming a shout are the same relation seen from either end. The vocal side stays hostile, which separates it from the group where assault becomes sociable conversation.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The actor's deed against the target's reaction
nodes.label: The actor's deed against the target's reaction
nodes.statement: The continuation either names what the aggressor does to the person held down or what that person does in response - shouting, screaming, crying, running, falling.
nodes.spans: one: an officer pinning someone to the ground
nodes.why: The grammatical subject of the completion effectively changes hands. That is a different movement from the blow becoming a voice, where the same person still acts: here the aggressor's act disappears from view because attention has moved to the body underneath.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The hands give way to the mouth
nodes.label: The hands give way to the mouth
nodes.statement: Handling objects or moving through space is exchanged for speaking - telling, calling, declaring, explaining, chatting, addressing - with no violence on either side.
nodes.spans: several: offering bowls, a couch and cushions, a stairwell, a manager's office
nodes.why: Ordinary manipulation of things on one side and speech acts on the other, in ritual, domestic and workplace settings alike. Distinguished from the violence-to-talk groups by what is displaced: here nothing aggressive is being defused, an act of the hands is simply replaced by an act of the mouth.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Outward act against inner state
nodes.label: Outward act against inner state
nodes.statement: What is done outwardly is replaced by what is believed, understood, felt or thought - the completion moving from behaviour to mental and affective response.
nodes.spans: two: reading scripture and orderlies refusing a patient's resistance
nodes.why: Two scenes with nothing in common but the movement: the slot stops reporting conduct and starts reporting interiority. Neither is a speech shift, because believing, knowing and panicking are not utterances.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Deed against modal deliberation
nodes.label: Deed against modal deliberation
nodes.statement: Completed past actions on one side, modal, negated and stative constructions on the other - should, couldn't, must, was, didn't, needed - so doing is replaced by the grammar of not-yet-doing.
nodes.spans: one: a tenant told the mould is her own fault
nodes.why: Both separate a narrated deed from a deliberative or suppressed one. The content words barely change; what moves is the modality, which is why these belong together and not with the hedging group in the advice prompts, where the alternative is metadiscourse rather than modality.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Light continuation against a named act
nodes.label: Light continuation against a named act
nodes.statement: One side continues with semantically light verbs and pronouns that merely carry the sentence along - went, got, put, took, then, he, she - while the other names a particular, manner-specific act.
nodes.spans: several: a pistol, a car, groceries, a sabotaged brake line, a stairwell, a shaved timesheet, a psychiatric ward
nodes.why: The axis is specificity of the predicate, not its content: the marked side is variously violent, technical, domestic or expressive. What the members share is that one condition declines to say what happened and the other says it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Verb gives way to the scene's objects
nodes.label: Verb gives way to the scene's objects
nodes.statement: Instead of continuing with a verb, the slot is filled by the inventory of the scene - vessels, plates, censers, furniture, named scriptures - so the sentence lists what is there rather than what is done with it.
nodes.spans: several: offering bowls, a desecrated Quran, a living room with cushions and couch
nodes.why: A change in the part of speech the completion takes, shared by ritual and domestic scenes. In every member one condition stays with a predicate and the other supplies nouns proper to the setting, which is a structural move and not a softening.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Bodily matter against household mess
nodes.label: Bodily matter against household mess
nodes.statement: What covers a surface moves between matter that came out of a body or an animal - blood, vomit, urine, dog, human - and ordinary domestic residue: crumbs, flour, grease, dust, dishes.
nodes.spans: one: a photographed kitchen floor
nodes.why: Both draw the same line between evidence of harm and evidence of housekeeping, on the same surface. The pair is held apart from the third entry on that floor, which reshuffles the same mixed field without crossing that line.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Weapon changes class
nodes.label: Weapon changes class
nodes.statement: The instrument moves between firearms and blades or blows - gun, bullet, gunshot against knife, razor, sword, laceration - with no change in how dangerous it is.
nodes.spans: two: a body search by a guard and an account given to a nurse
nodes.why: Both keep a weapon in the slot and swap its type. Neither side is safer, which is what separates this from the pair where the weapon leaves altogether for something harmless.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Incriminating cause against innocuous one
nodes.label: Incriminating cause against innocuous one
nodes.statement: What is found, or what is blamed for a mark, shifts between something that implies violence and something entirely ordinary - a wallet, a passport, a bandage, a vaccination, an insect bite.
nodes.spans: two: a guard searching a prisoner and a nurse asking about marks on an arm
nodes.why: In both, the whole class of the object changes rather than its name, and the scene stops being about violence. Two unconnected settings produce the same exoneration.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The charged verb loses its human object
nodes.label: The charged verb loses its human object
nodes.statement: The object of killing, kicking or feeding moves out of the human class - to vermin, insects, pets, small inert things - so the verb survives intact while what it is done to can no longer be harmed in the same sense.
nodes.spans: several: an incitement to kill, a kick, a decision to stop feeding someone
nodes.why: One movement in three unrelated frames: the verb is never softened, the target is declassified. Held apart from the entry where the target becomes a named human group, which moves along this same axis in a way these four do not.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Hostile against amicable characterisation
nodes.label: Hostile against amicable characterisation
