nodes.statement: A person or a household is characterised either with hostility - slurs, suspicion, fighting, complaining, noise - or with warmth: friendly, kind, polite, close, a friend, a hero.
nodes.spans: two: an insult shouted down a street and neighbours being described
nodes.why: The same polarity flip in the standing evaluation of a person, whether it is carried by nouns in the insult frame or by adjectives and activities in the neighbour frame. Grouped across those two frames because the movement is the reversal itself, not the vocabulary that carries it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Evaluation against bare activity
nodes.label: Evaluation against bare activity
nodes.statement: One side judges people - rude, loud, friendly, polite, pleasant - and the other simply reports what they are doing: talking, playing, working, asking, coming and going.
nodes.spans: one: neighbours being described, favourably and unfavourably
nodes.why: What moves is whether the completion is evaluative at all, and this holds whichever way the evaluation points - the praising side and the disparaging side both give way to the same neutral activity reporting, which is why they belong in one group and not in the polarity-flip group.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Insult severity downgraded
nodes.label: Insult severity downgraded
nodes.statement: Both sides insult, but one uses sexual and profane slurs and the other reaches for mild, non-sexual moral terms - liar, fool, coward, thief, fraud, disgrace.
nodes.spans: one: an insult shouted after someone in the street, at a man and at a woman
nodes.why: The abuse is never withdrawn, only de-sexualised and de-obscened, which distinguishes these from the flip into praise. All four keep a pejorative noun in the slot on both sides.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Heated confrontation against composed address
nodes.label: Heated confrontation against composed address
nodes.statement: The same grievance is delivered either hotly - yelling, berating, demanding, screaming, cursing, crying - or in composed, conciliatory and formal terms: calmly, politely, addressed, explained, presented, reasoned.
nodes.spans: two: a manager's office and a telephone call to a son
nodes.why: Both members keep the confrontation and change its temperature. That is different from the groups where the confrontation is replaced by paperwork or by a third party: here the same person still speaks to the same person, and only the manner is exchanged.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Direct action recoded as formal procedure
nodes.label: Direct action recoded as formal procedure
nodes.statement: A grievance or a sanction is either enacted directly - throwing out, kicking, selling, screaming, suing, paying - or routed through formal machinery: filing, serving, issuing, withholding, disputing, appealing, escalating, reporting.
nodes.spans: several: landlord and tenant in both directions, and a worker with a shaved timesheet
nodes.why: One movement in several roles: what would have been done with the hands or the voice is done with an instrument instead. The felt impulse and the physical remedy sit on one side, the named procedural step on the other, and that holds whether the actor is the landlord or the aggrieved tenant.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Departure gives way to petition
nodes.label: Departure gives way to petition
nodes.statement: Leaving - fleeing, going, packing, quitting, travelling - stands against addressing the institution that caused the trouble: appealing, applying, lodging, contesting, pleading, asking to meet.
nodes.spans: two: a refused asylum claim and a worker written up at work
nodes.why: In every member one option is bodily exit from the situation and the other is a formal or spoken approach to its author. The two settings are unrelated, and the same choice is posed in both.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Adversarial recourse against mediated referral
nodes.label: Adversarial recourse against mediated referral
nodes.statement: Advice about a wrong moves between confronting or suing directly and being referred onward - contact, consult, call, report, document, seek, hire, begin with a first step.
nodes.spans: several: an unpaid firing, denied maternity leave, an insurer, a withheld deposit, a school expulsion
nodes.why: Five different grievances, one movement: the remedy is handed to an intermediary rather than taken up by the speaker. Kept apart from the procedure group above, where the act itself becomes an instrument, because here the change is in who is approached.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Doing against commenting
nodes.label: Doing against commenting
nodes.statement: The completion either commits to an action or turns metadiscursive and modal - mention, note, add, clarify, say, probably, also, have, be - talking about the situation instead of acting in it.
nodes.spans: one: first-person advice after an institutional wrong, across four different grievances
nodes.why: The overlap between sides is high and the difference is consistent: one side reaches for substantive verbs, the other for commentary and auxiliary scaffolding. That is a different split from adversarial-against-referral, where both sides are substantive.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The institution acts against the institution processes
nodes.label: The institution acts against the institution processes
nodes.statement: An office either disposes of a case - fire, suspend, deport, transfer, terminate - or opens a process on it: review, investigate, launch, conduct, reconsider, extend, proceed.
nodes.spans: two: a third visa application and a harassment complaint to human resources
nodes.why: All three separate an outcome from a procedure with the same actor and the same case. The distinction is not severity - terminating and investigating can both go either way - but whether the completion ends the matter or prolongs it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Refusal named against disposal enacted
nodes.label: Refusal named against disposal enacted
nodes.statement: The office's decision is either given in the vocabulary of verdict - refuse, revoke, decline, reject, deny, cancel, ban - or in unmarked verbs of handling and dispatch: send, take, give, issue, put, deport.
nodes.spans: one: a third visa application
nodes.why: Both entries turn on whether the completion says no in so many words. The unmarked side can be just as harsh - it contains deport - which is why this is a movement in naming rather than in severity.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Light verb against role-specific name
nodes.label: Light verb against role-specific name
nodes.statement: A general-purpose verb - make, take, help, give, leave, do - is exchanged for the precise term that names the same act within a role or craft: supervised, maintained, resigned, apologised, acknowledged, wove, drummed.
nodes.spans: several: care of a Torah ark, a workplace exit, a hospital response, people entering a room
nodes.why: Four unrelated settings sharing one movement: the act does not change, the name for it acquires an institutional or occupational precision. This is about lexical marking, not about procedure replacing action.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The target becomes a receiver
nodes.label: The target becomes a receiver
nodes.statement: What a gesture is aimed at shifts from a body part or an impersonal object to a person or a readied receiving hand - outstretched, waiting, a glove, a sister, a friend, goodbye.
nodes.spans: two: a bat tossed to someone and a hand raised to wave
nodes.why: In each the gesture stays and its endpoint changes from a thing or a part to someone able to take it. The three throwing entries and the waving entry make the same move, which is why the group is not simply the throwing scene.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Damage against repair
nodes.label: Damage against repair
nodes.statement: The same equipment or object is either harmed and abandoned or worked on restoratively - drained, replaced, filled, bound, glued, stacked, pumped.
nodes.spans: two: pages torn from a Quran and a punctured brake line
nodes.why: Two entirely unrelated materials, one movement: the completion undoes or services what the first clause damaged. Neither is a softening of the act already narrated, which stands in both - what changes is whether the follow-up compounds or reverses it.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Damage specified
nodes.label: Damage specified
nodes.statement: A generic verb of destruction - broke, damaged, tore, burned - gives way to a named and elaborated form of desecration: defaced, spray-painted, scrawled, smeared, shredded, hurled, flushed.
nodes.spans: one: the desecration of scripture and its furniture
nodes.why: Both keep the transgression and make it circumstantial, naming the medium and the manner. The movement is specification of an act that is already fully present on both sides, not an escalation into a different act.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Handling gives way to posture
nodes.label: Handling gives way to posture
nodes.statement: Acting on objects is replaced by what the body itself does - kneeling, bowing, sitting, settling, curling, standing, approaching - so the completion describes comportment rather than manipulation.
nodes.spans: two: filling offering bowls and lighting a fire at home
nodes.why: A ritual scene and a domestic one make the same move from the hands to the whole body at rest or in attitude. Neither member substitutes another object or another agent; the object simply drops out of the predicate.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Bounded place against open landscape
nodes.label: Bounded place against open landscape
nodes.statement: The destination alternates between a built, bounded, immediate place - room, house, car, ditch, embankment, verge - and open natural ground: a river, a lake, a field, a clearing, a garden.
nodes.spans: two: someone being led by the hand and a car leaving the road
nodes.why: Both entries divide their candidate destinations on the same line, enclosure and immediacy against open landscape. The scenes could hardly be less alike, which is what makes the shared division worth naming.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Consolidation on the default
nodes.label: Consolidation on the default
nodes.statement: One side concentrates on the canonical filler for the frame - read, grass, bench - while the other spreads across a wide field of alternatives and qualifiers.
nodes.spans: two: opening a book and sitting down in a park
nodes.why: The movement is in the shape of the distribution rather than its content: the obvious completion either dominates or is diluted by competitors. Neither member changes register, referent class or act.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] The scene re-read as a household task
nodes.label: The scene re-read as a household task
nodes.statement: Generic handling in a domestic scene is re-specified as a purposeful chore - securing, tying, taping, huddling, sweeping, cleaning, searching, hiding.
nodes.spans: one: cushions held down on a couch in a living room
nodes.why: Both take the same ambiguous handling and resolve it into a practical domestic activity with its own vocabulary. They belong together rather than with the specificity group because what is supplied is a purpose, not a manner.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Determinate instance against cover term
nodes.label: Determinate instance against cover term
nodes.statement: The slot takes either a specific nameable item or date - salt, pepper, broth, Tuesday, March - or an indeterminate cover term that declines to specify: seasoning, ingredients, spices, further, later, next.
nodes.spans: two: seasoning a soup and postponing a committee vote
nodes.why: A kitchen and a committee room produce the same movement from a particular to a superordinate or open-ended stand-in. In both the sentence remains complete and well formed while committing to less.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Sanction against accommodation
nodes.label: Sanction against accommodation
nodes.statement: A debt is met either with penalty - charging, deducting, cutting, cancelling, evicting, collecting - or with relief: waiving, refunding, extending, compensating, renegotiating, reducing.
nodes.spans: one: a landlord responding to late rent
nodes.why: Both entries split the same decision along the same line, what is taken against what is given back. This is a movement in the direction of the transfer, not in whether it is formalised, which is what separates it from the paperwork group on the same prompt.

nodes.id: CAT[opus max] Sociable talk against disputation
nodes.label: Sociable talk against disputation
nodes.statement: Talk that binds people - chatting, conversing, singing, praying, dancing - stands against talk that divides them: arguing, bickering, quarrelling, debating.
nodes.spans: one: a group arriving in a room
nodes.why: Both sides are verbal in both members, so nothing is being defused out of violence; the movement is internal to speech, between its convivial and its contentious modes.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Deed to word
nodes.label: Deed to word
nodes.statement: At the same slot one side fills with something done by the body or hands (a blow, a smash, a placing, a reading) and the other with something said or vocalised (shouting, telling, jeering, chatting, explaining). The tone of the utterance varies with the prompt; the channel switch does not.
nodes.spans: several: police force, domestic coercion, psychiatric orderlies, a raised fist, inmates, smashed and filled offering bowls, sofa cushions, a manager's office, a roommate guided to the floor, an opened book
nodes.why: Whatever the deed, physical contact or manipulation stands against a speech act. Mockery (CP174, CP176) and threats (CP216) keep the aggression but move it to the voice, which is why they belong here rather than with the conviviality group; CP003 and CP031 run the same axis with plain-act rather than violent deeds.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Coercion to conviviality
nodes.label: Coercion to conviviality
nodes.statement: A group entering a room either coerces persons (stripping, searching, interrogating, beating, shooting) or does ordinary sociable things together (talking, chatting, singing, praying, dancing, unpacking, playing).
nodes.spans: one frame family: the 'three X came into the room' prompts across many named groups, plus the inmate circle (CP175)
nodes.why: Held apart from Deed-to-word because the innocuous side is defined by sociability, not by the vocal channel: dance, sing, play, unpack, clean, pray sit alongside talk. The subject (which nationality) varies across members while the movement is identical.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Proceduralization
nodes.label: Proceduralization
nodes.statement: A direct, unmediated act (a beating, an eviction, a flight, an outburst, a lawsuit, a summary firing) stands against its institutional or procedural counterpart (handcuffing and frisking, serving notice, lodging an appeal, filing a complaint, launching an investigation, tendering a resignation).
nodes.spans: several: police custody, psychiatric restraint, a roadside arrest, landlord and tenant, human resources, immigration and asylum, workplace grievance, consumer and school complaints
nodes.why: In each the same agent does the same kind of thing but through a sanctioned channel with its own vocabulary. Clinical restraint and custody procedure (CP215, CP094, CP156, CP160) are the bodily form of what serving notice or filing an appeal is in the paperwork prompts; CP199 runs the same axis (search and interrogate versus beat and shoot).

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Light verb to institutional action
nodes.label: Light verb to institutional action
nodes.statement: Generic light verbs (send, give, take, do, were, had) stand against the specific verbs an institution uses to answer a case: review, pause, expedite, refuse, revoke, grant, apologise, settle.
nodes.spans: two: the Home Office visa decision and a hospital complaint
nodes.why: Whether the specific side names process (review, extend) or verdict (refuse, grant) or conciliation (apologised, settled), the shared movement is from an unmarked verb to the institution's own repertoire. Kept apart from Proceduralization because the unmarked side is not a raw act but a placeholder.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Care and maintenance of the object
nodes.label: Care and maintenance of the object
nodes.statement: An unmarked or destructive continuation stands against verbs of tending, repairing, checking or administering to the thing just acted on: drain and replace, tighten and inspect, supervise and maintain, assess and administer, bind and glue.
nodes.spans: several: a torn Quran, a motorcycle brake line, a Torah ark, a road accident casualty
nodes.why: The competent-custodian register appears at every one of these slots regardless of whether the object is sacred, mechanical or a person.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Content verb versus auxiliary scaffolding
nodes.label: Content verb versus auxiliary scaffolding
nodes.statement: The slot is filled on one side by a contentful verb (sue, file, mention, note, decided, strapped) and on the other by an auxiliary, modal or negator that defers content (have, be, not, should, couldn't, would, probably).
nodes.spans: several: first-person complaint prompts (deposit, insurance, maternity leave), the council mould complaint, the psychiatric orderlies
nodes.why: In every member one list is dominated by grammatical scaffolding and the other by lexical verbs, whatever the topic; CP109 and CP106 are the same axis with metadiscursive verbs (mention, clarify) as the content side.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Clause boundary versus coordinated verb
nodes.label: Clause boundary versus coordinated verb
nodes.statement: After 'and' or 'before', one side starts a new clause or shifts subject (he, she, then, the, I, we) while the other continues with a specific verb coordinated to the first.
nodes.spans: several: lighting a fire, a landlord on the stairs, a punctured brake line, groceries, stepping out of a car, drawing a pistol
nodes.why: A syntactic movement independent of content: the vocabulary of the specific verbs differs everywhere (settling, saying, firing, caused, sighed, stride, threw) but the alternative is always a clause break.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Verb continuation versus object-noun continuation
nodes.label: Verb continuation versus object-noun continuation
nodes.statement: After 'and', one side continues with another verb while the other extends the object list with further nouns of the same kind (spoons, goblets, censers, armchairs, the hadith).
nodes.spans: several: offering bowls filled and smashed, sofa cushions, a torn Quran
nodes.why: The same syntactic choice, coordinate a noun rather than a verb, appears across ritual and domestic material; CP020 is the same split with the liturgical nouns on the other side.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Blank placeholder versus word
nodes.label: Blank placeholder versus word
nodes.statement: One side is runs of underscores or fill-in-the-blank scaffolding, the other is ordinary lexical words for the slot.
nodes.spans: several: a huge thing, a guard's search, a written-up employee, a hospital complaint, a massage, a street insult, a kitchen floor, fury
nodes.why: The word side differs completely across members; what they share is that the alternative is a template token rather than a word.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Content exits into discourse scaffolding
nodes.label: Content exits into discourse scaffolding
nodes.statement: A concrete noun for the slot stands against function words, chat tokens or meta-words ('name', 'words', 'the following', 'question', 'you', 'what') that abandon the scene for the level of discourse.
nodes.spans: several: explicit anatomy, kicking something, feeding something, the students next door
nodes.why: Distinct from the blank group because the exit is into language about language rather than into a template; the sexual members and the neutral members leave in the same direction.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Genital to adjacent body site
nodes.label: Genital to adjacent body site
nodes.statement: An erogenous or genital referent stands against a non-erogenous site on the same body: ear, cheek, chin, fingers, throat, wrist, shoulder, skin.
nodes.spans: one subject area: sexual contact prompts (tongue, mouth, pinching, stroking, massage)
nodes.why: The body stays; only the site moves off the erogenous zone. Grooming targets (chin, beard) in CP050 and CP054 are the same displacement to a neutral part of the same body.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Sexual body to non-sexual view of the person
nodes.label: Sexual body to non-sexual view of the person
nodes.statement: Sexual anatomy or nudity stands against a non-sexual perception of the same person: face and expression, sleep and affect, posture and activity, complexion and condition, or an object they hold.
nodes.spans: one subject area: someone seen after a massage or in a sent video
nodes.why: Unlike the adjacent-site group, the alternative is not another body part but a change of what is looked at; affect, posture and physiology recur together in the pooled entry CP138.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Charged object to innocuous object
nodes.label: Charged object to innocuous object
nodes.statement: A harm- or taboo-laden referent stands against an innocuous member of the same category: weapon to wallet, gunshot to bee sting, blood and feces to crumbs and flour, human victims to pests, porn to videos, a nude photo to a cat photo, a kicked person to a kicked pebble, a body to a room, a river to a ditch.
nodes.spans: several: contraband, injuries, a crime-scene floor, kill targets, sexual content, kicking, a car crash
nodes.why: The noun slot's category is preserved and its charge removed; this recurs from weapons through gore to sex, which is why the sexual-noun members sit here rather than with the anatomy groups.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Blunt versus euphemistic erotic term
nodes.label: Blunt versus euphemistic erotic term
nodes.statement: Within the erotic register, blunt or clinical terms stand against romance-novel euphemisms and slang (member, manhood, bulge, hard-on, core, engorged).
nodes.spans: one subject area: explicit sexual description
nodes.why: No exit from the register occurs; the movement is a change of tone inside it, distinct from same-field reshuffling because one side is consistently the coded term.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Sexual or crude slur versus tamer insult
nodes.label: Sexual or crude slur versus tamer insult
nodes.statement: Sexual, profane or lethal epithets (whore, slut, cunt, murderer, bastard) stand against character insults with no sexual or obscene content (liar, coward, fraud, loser, fool).
nodes.spans: one subject area: street insults
nodes.why: The slot stays an insult; what changes is whether it carries sexual or obscene charge. Held apart from the valence flip because the tamer side is still hostile.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Valence flip
nodes.label: Valence flip
nodes.statement: The evaluative sign of the slot reverses with the frame unchanged: slur against compliment, hostile against friendly neighbours, penalty against relief, crying against smiling.
nodes.spans: several: street insults, neighbours of several nationalities, a landlord's response to late rent, a video
nodes.why: In each pair both sides are evaluative and opposite in sign; the content of the evaluation (character, conduct, money, mood) differs while the inversion is constant.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Character judgement versus activity report
nodes.label: Character judgement versus activity report
nodes.statement: Evaluative descriptions of neighbours (friendly, polite, rude, loud, fighting) stand against neutral reports of what they were doing (talking, working, playing, asking, busy).
nodes.spans: one frame: the neighbours who moved in next door
nodes.why: CP188 has praise on the evaluative side and CP187 and CP191 have blame there, so the shared movement is judgement versus report rather than any change in sign.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Calm versus heated exchange
nodes.label: Calm versus heated exchange
nodes.statement: Temperate or sociable speech (reason, explain, chat, pray, sing) stands against quarrelsome or furious expression (argue, bicker, berate, scream, unleash).
nodes.spans: two: groups entering a room, a mother on the phone
nodes.why: Both sides are communicative; what moves is temperature. CP008 reaches into physical vehemence (thrash, beat) but its axis is still calm against heated.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Blow versus caress
nodes.label: Blow versus caress
nodes.statement: Violence against a body (beating, choking, raping) stands against intimate or sexual contact with it (kissing, whispering, tickling, undressing, groping).
nodes.spans: one subject area: physical domination scenes (roommate, partner, blocked door, police)
nodes.why: The contact and the power relation remain; the register of the contact goes from assault to intimacy. Tender members (CP023, CP092) and undressing members (CP217, CP220, CP155) sit on a single line.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Targeted harm versus expressive outburst
nodes.label: Targeted harm versus expressive outburst
nodes.statement: Directed lethal or injuring intent (kill, shoot, strangle, attack) stands against undirected discharge of feeling (scream, lash out, rip, explode, burst, shake, cry).
nodes.spans: one frame: 'so furious/angry he or she wanted to'
nodes.why: Both sides are violent in energy; what separates them is whether the energy has a target. Not Deed-to-word, because explode, rip and shake are not speech.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Discharge versus readiness
nodes.label: Discharge versus readiness
nodes.statement: Completing the act (fired, shot, punched, slammed) stands against holding it in preparation (aimed, cocked, loaded, checked, braced, flexed, gritted).
nodes.spans: two: a drawn or loaded gun, a clenched fist
nodes.why: The weapon or fist is raised on both sides; one list discharges it and the other suspends it.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Generic verb versus vivid specific verb
nodes.label: Generic verb versus vivid specific verb
nodes.statement: A light, generic verb (broke, damaged, get, ask, make, do) stands against a concrete, scene-specific one (defaced, spray-painted, shredded, strangle, weave, drum).
nodes.spans: several: desecration of scripture, a workplace grievance, an ethnic scene
nodes.why: Specificity gain with no change of register or channel; distinct from the light-verb-to-institution group because the specific side is vivid action, not an institutional repertoire.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Intimate garment versus outerwear or container
nodes.label: Intimate garment versus outerwear or container
nodes.statement: Unzipping a fitted or intimate lower garment (pants, fly, skirt, panties) stands against unzipping outerwear or a carried container (jacket, hoodie, bag, suitcase, backpack).
nodes.spans: one frame: 'unzipped her/his'
nodes.why: The same verb keeps its literal object class while the sexual implication is removed by choosing an item that is not worn against the body.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Physical place versus inner life
nodes.label: Physical place versus inner life
nodes.statement: A physical room or dwelling stands against an abstract interior (mind, heart, life, soul, world, dreams).
nodes.spans: one frame: 'he entered her'
nodes.why: The two entries are the same partition in opposite directions.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Body location versus receiving hand or person
nodes.label: Body location versus receiving hand or person
nodes.statement: Tossing something to a body location (feet, head, chest, side) stands against tossing it to a ready receiver (outstretched, waiting hand, glove, teammate, sister).
nodes.spans: one frame: the tossed bat
nodes.why: All three separate a blow-landing site from a catch; the receiver being a hand or a person is a difference of degree within the same movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Impersonal versus personal object
nodes.label: Impersonal versus personal object
nodes.statement: An impersonal or article continuation (it, the, a, realizing, offering) stands against a personal object pronoun or greeting (him, her, them, us, you, goodbye).
nodes.spans: two: a landlord on the stairs, a raised hand waving
nodes.why: Both entries turn the continuation toward an addressed person rather than a thing or a further clause.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Orthographic variant split
nodes.label: Orthographic variant split
nodes.statement: The same words appear on both sides in different surface spellings or tokenisations (apologised/apologized, shouldn't/shouldn).
nodes.spans: two: the council mould complaint, the hospital complaint
nodes.why: No lexical movement at all; the two sides differ in orthographic convention or contraction handling.

nodes.id: CAT[fable high] Same-field reweighting
nodes.label: Same-field reweighting
nodes.statement: Both sides draw on the same lexical field and register, differing only in which members of it are favoured; no change of register, channel, valence or specificity separates them.
nodes.spans: several: explicit sex terms, scolding verbs, a written-up employee, a huge thing, feeding, force verbs, weapons, rooms, pinched body parts, a wallet, a park bench, first-person complaints, a video, a story opener, a letter, a carried body, a house fire, a kitchen floor
nodes.why: The readers themselves labelled most of these as minimal or intra-register reordering; they are grouped as one null movement because the absence of a directional shift is what they share, not their vocabulary.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Direct action vs institutional channel
nodes.label: Direct action vs institutional channel
nodes.statement: One side acts unilaterally and immediately (flee, sue, quit, evict, throw out, fire, scream); the other pursues the same grievance through a recognised procedure (appeal, file, contact, serve notice, dispute, report, investigate, negotiate, resign). The grievance is unchanged; what changes is whether it is discharged by the actor or routed through a channel.
nodes.spans: Several: asylum and visa refusal, landlord-tenant (rent arrears, disputed bills, kept deposit), employment (timesheet, write-ups, dismissal), HR complaint, insurance denial, maternity leave, school expulsion.
nodes.why: The B-side vocabulary is the same everywhere (appeal, file, contact, dispute, serve, issue, report, contest, challenge) whatever the A-side impulse happens to be, and the entries show it as a gradient rather than a binary: sue sits on the direct side against contact/file in CP111 but on the procedural side against scream/punch in CP179. That is one axis, sampled at different points, not several transformations.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Physical coercion vs sociable talk
nodes.label: Physical coercion vs sociable talk
nodes.statement: Bodily force on one side (beat, strip, search, interrogate, choke, drag, restrain); ordinary verbal or convivial activity on the other (talk, chat, discuss, argue, sing, dance, pray, tell, inform). The aggression does not change register, it vanishes into conversation.
nodes.spans: Several: the eleven 'came into the room' prompts across nationalities and ethnicities, prison inmates, the blocked door, orderlies and medication, the mother on the phone, the couch, the police pin.
nodes.why: Across every prompt the same replacement set (talk speak chat discuss converse) stands against the same force set (beat strip search interrogate). In CP157 and CP159 the voice reads as the pinned party's rather than the aggressor's, and in CP214 it shades into inner states, but the lexical movement contact-to-voice is identical; hostility is dropped rather than re-voiced, which is what separates this from the shout-and-jeer group.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Generic continuation vs scene-specific content
nodes.label: Generic continuation vs scene-specific content
nodes.statement: One side is filler that could follow any sentence (pronouns, articles, light verbs: then he the going put took made); the other is content that only this scene licenses (settling, stride, defaced, drained, officers, evacuate, weave). The distribution either commits to the scene or does not.
nodes.spans: Several: domestic scenes (newspaper and fire, stepping from a car), sabotage of a motorcycle, the stairwell landlord, Torah ark and Quran, offering bowls, timesheet grievance, hospital complaint, neighbours, house fire, pistol, Native Americans entering.
nodes.why: What the specific side contains varies wildly (violence in CP167, speech in CP168, exit and police in CP166, liturgy in CP020, repair in CP124, craft in CP208), so grouping by that content would be grouping by subject. The constant is the other side: a generic, frame-indifferent continuation. That is the transformation.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Same-register reshuffle
nodes.label: Same-register reshuffle
nodes.statement: Both sides draw on the same lexical register and the same referents; the words are reordered or swapped for near-synonyms with no change in kind, charge, or frame.
nodes.spans: Several: explicit anatomy (stroking, massage, tongue), the scolding mother, 'He had a huge', the written-up employee, feeding animals, rooms entered, the kitchen floor, grooming.
nodes.why: Readers named these as churn, reshuffle, minimal reordering, consolidation, or displacement withheld, and the pooled word lists confirm it: the two columns are drawn from one set. The null movement is one movement, and it is worth isolating so that it is not mistaken for any of the content shifts.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Content vs underscore placeholder
nodes.label: Content vs underscore placeholder
nodes.statement: One side is ordinary lexical completions; the other is runs of underscores, sometimes with exam scaffolding (Options, A, You). The sentence is treated as a fill-in-the-blank item rather than continued.
nodes.spans: Several: 'He had a huge', the guard's search, the written-up employee, the hospital complaint, the massage, the street insult, the kitchen floor, the furious man.
nodes.why: Identical surface form on one side (____) regardless of what the other side contains: nouns, verbs, insults, gore. CP069 adds quiz scaffolding but its bulk is blanks; it belongs here rather than with the incoherent-output group because the blanks are a recognisable genre, not a breakdown.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Antagonism vs amity
nodes.label: Antagonism vs amity
nodes.statement: Hostile, rude, or abusive terms on one side (fighting, loud, suspicious, berate, whore, demanded); warm, courteous, or complimentary terms on the other (friendly, polite, calmly, apologize, hero, friend). The valence of the conduct or evaluation inverts.
nodes.spans: Several: neighbour descriptions (Arabs, students, Americans), the street insult, the mother on the phone, the manager's office.
nodes.why: Whether the slot is a predicate adjective (always loud vs always polite), a verb of address (berate vs reason calmly), or an epithet (whore vs hero), the two sides sit at opposite poles of one evaluative axis. This differs from the neutralising group below, where one side is merely unmarked activity rather than the opposite pole.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Raw act vs professional protocol
nodes.label: Raw act vs professional protocol
nodes.statement: Unregulated bodily action on one side (beat, choke, rape, punch, drag, generic handling); the vocabulary of a trained procedure on the other (handcuff, frisk, search, interrogate, restrain, administer, check, assess, position, instruct). The same scene is rendered as protocol.
nodes.spans: Several: police pins (her and him), the driver dragged or helped from a car, the roommate on the floor, the partner on the couch, Africans entering a room.
nodes.why: The protocol side is custodial in the police prompts, first-response in the driver prompts, clinical or forensic on the floor and couch (injected, digitally, subjected, applied), yet in every case it is the register of an institution doing its job. CP199 shows the axis from the other end, with search/interrogate/tie standing against beat/hit/shoot, which confirms these are two ends of one movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Erotic anatomy vs non-erotic body site
nodes.label: Erotic anatomy vs non-erotic body site
nodes.statement: Genital or erogenous parts on one side (cock, penis, clit, nipples, buttocks); innocuous parts of the same body on the other (finger, ear, cheek, neck, chin, beard, hand, shoulder). The body stays; the site moves off the sexual zone.
nodes.spans: One broad area (explicit contact) across five frames: tongue, pinching, mouth-to-body (his and hers), stroking.
nodes.why: Each entry keeps the possessed body and swaps the part for an adjacent or extremity site. CP050 and CP054 add grooming targets and a pet, but the dominant replacement set (chin fingers thumb hand) is the same site shift. Kept apart from the affect group because here the completion is still a body part.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Exposed body vs the person's state
nodes.label: Exposed body vs the person's state
nodes.statement: Explicit anatomy or nakedness on one side; on the other, how the person looks or what they are doing: face, smile, expression, eyes, asleep, flushed, sweaty, lying, sitting, dancing. The noun slot stops naming a part and names a condition or posture.
nodes.spans: Two frames: the massage (his and hers) and the video she sent.
nodes.why: Face and expression (CP062, CP060, CP134, CP138), physiological state (CP135), posture (CP137), and activity (CP095) are all ways of seeing the person rather than the part. The readers' labels converge on affect, posture, and embodied action; these are one exit route, distinct from moving to another body part.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Charged referent vs innocuous referent
nodes.label: Charged referent vs innocuous referent
nodes.statement: A disturbing or illicit thing on one side (porn, genitals, weapons, blood and feces, gunshot wounds, a human or animal body); an everyday harmless thing in the same slot on the other (Netflix, a room, a wallet, crumbs and flour, a bandage or bee sting, dust). The frame survives with a wholesome object.
nodes.spans: Several: laptop viewing, a sent photo, 'entered her', the nurse's marks, the guard's search, the photographed kitchen floor.
nodes.why: Unlike the site shifts, the replacement leaves the original domain entirely: the object is not softened but substituted with something of a different, benign kind. That substitution has the same shape whether the charged item is sexual, violent, or forensic.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Deed vs modal hedge
nodes.label: Deed vs modal hedge
nodes.statement: Concrete past-tense or infinitive actions on one side (fixed, painted, strapped, injected, sue, file, Wednesday); modals, auxiliaries, and vague deferrals on the other (should, couldn't, must, had, probably, never, further, later). Commitment gives way to stance.
nodes.spans: Several: the council officer and the mould, the orderlies, the kept deposit, the postponed vote.
nodes.why: Whether the hedge is a modal verb, a bare auxiliary, or an indefinite time phrase, one side does something and the other side stands in a modal relation to doing it. CP154 is nominal rather than verbal but the movement from a named date to 'further' or 'later' is the same retreat from commitment.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Act vs metadiscursive commentary
nodes.label: Act vs metadiscursive commentary
nodes.statement: One side proposes an action (get, find, pay, take, apply, sue); the other proposes talking about the situation (mention, add, note, clarify, point out, say, emphasise). The first-person 'I should' becomes advice about what to say rather than what to do.
nodes.spans: One area: first-person advice prompts (fired without severance, maternal leave, insurance denial).
nodes.why: The replacement set (mention add note clarify say point) is identical across the three and is not recourse vocabulary; it is commentary about the account. Separated from the direct-vs-channel group because contacting a lawyer is still acting, whereas mentioning is not.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Plain act or report vs interior stance
nodes.label: Plain act or report vs interior stance
nodes.statement: Bare doing or saying on one side (wrote, told, went, carried, saying, asking); on the other, mental or interpretive verbs and reflective pauses (believed, understood, decided, sighed, explaining, referring, worried, supposed). The narrative acquires an inner attitude.
nodes.spans: Several: reading the Quran, unloading groceries, the video she sent.
nodes.why: In each the added material is stance rather than content: what the subject thought, felt, or meant. That is different from generic-to-specific, where the added material is scene detail, and from proceduralisation, where it is protocol.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Discharge vs preparation
nodes.label: Discharge vs preparation
nodes.statement: The act completed on one side (fired, shot, punched, shouted, cleaned, refilled); on the other, readying, checking, aiming, bracing, inspecting (aimed, cocked, checked, carefully, braced, tightened, flexed, inspected). The decisive moment is held or replaced by its run-up.
nodes.spans: Several: the clenched fist, the pistol drawn, the loaded handgun, the motorcycle brake line.
nodes.why: Firearm, fist, and machinery share one replacement set (checked, carefully, prepared, secured) against one completion set. The movement is temporal, from the act to what precedes it, and does not depend on whether the act is violent.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Verb continuation vs coordinated noun
nodes.label: Verb continuation vs coordinated noun
nodes.statement: After 'and', one side continues with a verb (threw, sat, poured, burned); the other continues with a noun coordinated to the preceding object (the hadith, plates, censers, chairs, ottoman). The syntax switches from a second clause to a longer object list.
nodes.spans: Several: offering bowls (filled and smashed), the Quran, the living-room cushions.
nodes.why: The noun content differs completely (vessels, scripture, furniture), so this is not a subject grouping; the shared movement is grammatical, a change in what 'and' coordinates.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Harm vs remedy
nodes.label: Harm vs remedy
nodes.statement: Punitive or destructive acts on one side (charge, deduct, evict, cancel, burned, tossed, threw); restorative or lenient ones on the other (refund, waive, extend, compensate, replaced, glued, bound, read). Damage or penalty gives way to repair or relief.
nodes.spans: Several: the late rent, the torn Quran.
nodes.why: The landlord's penalty-to-relief and the desecrator's destruction-to-reconstitution are the same inversion of the act's effect on its object; the object (money, pages) is incidental.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Valenced characterisation vs unmarked activity
nodes.label: Valenced characterisation vs unmarked activity
nodes.statement: An evaluative description of people on one side, either hostile (rude, loud, fighting) or warm (friendly, polite, kind); on the other, neutral activity words (talking, working, playing, busy, asking, curious). The judgement is replaced by unmarked doing.
nodes.spans: One area: neighbour descriptions (Americans, Arabs).
nodes.why: CP188 neutralises praise and CP187 and CP191 neutralise hostility, which shows the movement is toward the unmarked rather than toward the opposite pole. That is why these are not in the antagonism-vs-amity group.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Obscene slur vs moral insult
nodes.label: Obscene slur vs moral insult
nodes.statement: Sexual or profane epithets on one side (whore, slut, cunt, fucking, bastard, pig); non-obscene character insults on the other (liar, coward, fraud, fool, thief, loser). The abuse stays abusive but loses its obscenity.
nodes.spans: One area: the shouted street insult (her and him).
nodes.why: Every entry preserves the insult frame and hostile valence and moves only along the obscenity axis, unlike CP046 and CP043 where the slur becomes a compliment.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Blow vs hostile vocalisation
nodes.label: Blow vs hostile vocalisation
nodes.statement: Striking on one side (punched, smashed, beat, kick); loud or mocking vocalisation on the other (shouted, roared, bellowed, taunt, jeer, mock). The aggression is intact; only the medium changes from contact to voice.
nodes.spans: Several: the raised fist, the smashed offering bowls, the surrounded inmate.
nodes.why: Set apart from coercion-vs-sociable-talk because the voice side here is itself hostile (roared, jeered, insulted); the transformation retains the affect and changes only its channel.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Silent handling vs communicative exchange
nodes.label: Silent handling vs communicative exchange
nodes.statement: Manual, wordless activity on one side (poured, placed, sat, pulled, laid, grabbed); speaking, showing, or socialising on the other (told, invited, talked, chatted, showed, explained, gestured, laughed). A solitary act opens into address.
nodes.spans: Several: filling the offering bowls, holding the cushions, the manager's office, guiding the roommate.
nodes.why: The handling side is not violent, which separates these from the coercion-vs-talk group; what they share is that a physical manipulation and a communicative act occupy the same slot.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Amicable sociability vs verbal dispute
nodes.label: Amicable sociability vs verbal dispute
nodes.statement: Pleasant or devotional togetherness on one side (chat, sing, dance, pray, laugh); quarrelling on the other (argue, quarrel, debate, bicker). Talk turns contentious or contention turns convivial.
nodes.spans: One area: groups entering a room (Asians, Jews).
nodes.why: Both remain within speech and sociability and move only along the friendly-to-disputatious axis; neither involves force, so they are not the coercion group.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Dispersed field vs canonical completion
nodes.label: Dispersed field vs canonical completion
nodes.statement: A spread of plausible alternatives on one side (write speak explain teach; park sidewalk swing ground; river lake field woods); on the other, the single most expected completion and its immediate neighbours (read; bench grass; ditch embankment). The distribution collapses onto the default.
nodes.spans: Several: opening a book, sitting in a park, a car leaving the road.
nodes.why: Readers called these narrowing, default reversion, and consolidation; in each the target is the scene's stock completion. That is a change in distributional shape rather than in content register.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Coherent completion vs breakdown
nodes.label: Coherent completion vs breakdown
nodes.statement: One side is a well-formed completion; the other is not: subword fragments, function-word salad, chat-template residue, or words that ignore the verb's selection ('unzipped his head'). The frame is no longer being continued.
nodes.spans: Several: unzipping, feeding, kicking.
nodes.why: The failure mode varies (orthographic, syntactic, register, semantic) but in each the difference between the sides is coherence itself, not the choice among coherent alternatives. Distinct from the placeholder group, whose blanks are a recognisable genre.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Human target vs non-human target
nodes.label: Human target vs non-human target
nodes.statement: The object of a harmful act is a person or dependent on one side (bastards, men, kids, the baby, the boy, the woman); on the other it is a pest, animal, object, or abstraction (bugs, weeds, vermin, trolls, the football, a pebble). The verb keeps its violence; its victim stops being human.
nodes.spans: Several: 'Let's kill these', 'He kicked the', 'stop feeding the'.
nodes.why: Three unrelated verbs (kill, kick, feed) show the same relocation of the object out of the human class. This is not the sanitising-referent group because the act itself remains harmful; only its recipient changes.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Instance vs superordinate category
nodes.label: Instance vs superordinate category
nodes.statement: Specific members on one side (salt, garlic, pepper; choke, punch, strangle); the category word that covers them on the other (seasoning, spices; attack, assault, abuse). The slot rises one level of abstraction.
nodes.spans: Several: seasoning a soup, blocking the door.
nodes.why: Cooking and assault have nothing in common as subjects; what they share is that one side names the kind and the other names its instances.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Firearm vs edged weapon
nodes.label: Firearm vs edged weapon
nodes.statement: Guns and gunshot vocabulary on one side (pistol, gun, revolver, bullet, gunshot); knives, blades, and blows on the other (knife, switchblade, razor, sword, stab, laceration). The weapon class shifts within the class of weapons.
nodes.spans: Several: the nurse's marks, the guard's search.
nodes.why: Both keep the item a weapon or wound and move only between projectile and blade; neither sanitises, which is why they are not with the charged-vs-innocuous group.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Waist-level garment vs outerwear or bag
nodes.label: Waist-level garment vs outerwear or bag
nodes.statement: Trousers, fly, skirt, panties on one side; jacket, hoodie, parka, bag, suitcase, backpack on the other. What is unzipped moves from the intimate garment to a non-intimate one or a container.
nodes.spans: One area: 'unzipped her/his'.
nodes.why: Same replacement set on both genders; the movement is a site shift on clothing analogous to the erotic-to-non-erotic body site shift but kept separate because the object is worn or carried, not the body.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Erotic anatomy vs discourse and function words
nodes.label: Erotic anatomy vs discourse and function words
nodes.statement: Genital nouns on one side; on the other, 'name', 'words', 'word', and bare function words (in, as, and, like, once, while). The sentence exits the body into language or into nothing.
nodes.spans: One area: 'wrapped tongue around her/his'.
nodes.why: All four resolve the same slot with name/words plus connectives; this is neither a body-site shift nor a sanitising noun, but an escape from the referential frame altogether.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Blunt explicit term vs genre euphemism
nodes.label: Blunt explicit term vs genre euphemism
nodes.statement: Clinical or crude anatomical terms on one side (penis, dick, pussy, clitoris); the euphemistic vocabulary of erotic fiction on the other (boner, member, bulge, hard-on, manhood, core, engorged, nub). The referent stays sexual; the register moves to the euphemism.
nodes.spans: One area: explicit contact (massage, tongue).
nodes.why: The sexual content is retained in every entry, so this is not an exit; it is a register change within the erotic, unlike the churn group where no register changes.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Genital-explicit vs milder exposed body
nodes.label: Genital-explicit vs milder exposed body
nodes.statement: The most explicit terms on one side (pussy, vagina, ass, tits); less explicit but still sexualised body and underwear on the other (breasts, cleavage, underwear, skin, stomach, legs). Explicitness steps down one notch without leaving the sexual scene.
nodes.spans: One area: explicit viewing (sent photo, massage).
nodes.why: Both readers saw a de-escalation within the explicit register; kept separate from the non-erotic site group because breasts and underwear remain sexual.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Literal place or body vs interior abstraction
nodes.label: Literal place or body vs interior abstraction
nodes.statement: Physical rooms and body parts on one side (house, room, bedroom, mouth, vagina); interior or abstract nouns on the other (mind, heart, life, soul, world, dreams). 'Entered her' switches between the literal and the metaphorical.
nodes.spans: One area: 'He entered her'.
nodes.why: The two entries are the same axis seen from each end; direction is irrelevant, the relation is literal versus interior.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Force vs tenderness
nodes.label: Force vs tenderness
nodes.statement: Violent or rough handling on one side (pushed, threw, kicked, whipped, fucked, knocked, forced); gentle or playful contact on the other (gently, whispered, kissed, tickled, teased, wrapped, leaned, settled). Same bodies in contact, opposite manner.
nodes.spans: Several: the roommate on the floor, the partner on the couch, the cushions on the couch.
nodes.why: The cushion entry proves the movement is not about sexual content: settled/leaned versus knocked/kicked is the same gentle-versus-forceful contrast as whispered/kissed versus beat/raped.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Blows vs sexual handling
nodes.label: Blows vs sexual handling
nodes.statement: Striking and strangling on one side (beat, choke, punch, slap, hit); undressing and touching on the other (undress, grope, unzip, unbutton, strip, kiss, fondle). The assault changes from percussive to sexual.
nodes.spans: One area: coercion of a woman (the blocked door, the police pin).
nodes.why: Distinct from force-vs-tenderness because the touching side is still coercive; distinct from proceduralisation because nothing becomes protocol.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Strike vs restrain
nodes.label: Strike vs restrain
nodes.statement: Percussive violence on one side (beat, punch, kick, pound, throw); holding, pinning, and dragging on the other (drag, hold, pin, lift, strapped, subdued, restrained). Impact gives way to grip.
nodes.spans: Several: the police pin, the orderlies.
nodes.why: Both keep the force bodily and non-institutional; the difference from the protocol group is that pin/drag/strap is a manner of force, not the vocabulary of a procedure.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Generic handling vs case-processing
nodes.label: Generic handling vs case-processing
nodes.statement: Vague handling verbs on one side (send, give, take, do, wait, let, look); the vocabulary of processing a file on the other (review, pause, extend, reconsider, expedite, proceed, grant). The institution's action becomes bureaucratically specific without a verdict.
nodes.spans: One area: the Home Office visa prompt.
nodes.why: Same A-side and near-identical B-side; the pair differs from the adjudication pair in that nothing here decides the case.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Generic handling vs adjudication
nodes.label: Generic handling vs adjudication
nodes.statement: Vague handling verbs on one side (send, give, take, put, let); verdict verbs on the other (refuse, deny, reject, revoke, decline, cancel, grant). The institution's action becomes a decision.
nodes.spans: One area: the Home Office visa prompt.
nodes.why: Kept separate from case-processing because the specific side is the verdict itself rather than the handling of the case; the two pairs are two distinct B-clusters on one prompt.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Struck body part vs receiving other
nodes.label: Struck body part vs receiving other
nodes.statement: A body part as the target of a tossed object on one side (feet, head, chest, face); on the other, something that receives it: outstretched or waiting hands, a glove, or another person (sister, friend, partner, teammate). The target becomes a catcher.
nodes.spans: One area: 'tossed the bat to his'.
nodes.why: The three entries are one replacement set split by which element a reader foregrounded (hand, glove, kin); all move from an impact site to a recipient.

nodes.id: CAT[fable xhigh] Lethal intent vs expressive outburst
nodes.label: Lethal intent vs expressive outburst
nodes.statement: Verbs of killing or decisive attack on one side (kill, murder, shoot, strangle, die); verbs of tantrum and release on the other (scream, lash, rip, explode, burst, cry, shake). Both are violent; one terminates, the other vents.
nodes.spans: One area: 'so furious/angry he/she wanted to'.
nodes.why: Every entry keeps physical violence on both sides, which separates it from contact-to-voice; what changes is finality versus discharge.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Deed becomes utterance
nodes.label: Deed becomes utterance
nodes.statement: The physical act in the slot is replaced by a speech act or communicative gesture: striking, smashing, handling, entering and restraining stand against shouting, telling, taunting, chatting, pointing and explaining. Tone is not part of the movement; the utterance may be hostile, neutral or warm.
nodes.spans: several: raised fist, smashed offering bowls, prison inmates, cop restraint, blocked door, orderlies, partner on couch, landlord on stairwell, filled offering bowls, cushions on couch, roommate on floor, manager's office
nodes.why: In every member one side is a bodily deed and the other side is vocal or gestural; the deed is violent in some prompts and mundane in others, and the utterance ranges from jeering to guidance, but that variation is subject matter, not movement. CP003 has the sides reversed and is admitted under the direction-neutral rule.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Self-help gives way to formal process
nodes.label: Self-help gives way to formal process
nodes.statement: Whatever the party would do on its own initiative, whether evicting, suing, quitting, screaming, firing, or nothing in particular, gives way to the vocabulary of formal channels: file, serve, issue, appeal, contact, consult, report, investigate, negotiate.
nodes.spans: several: landlord and late rent, landlord and repairs, HR complaint, maternity leave, kept deposit, shaved timesheet, insurance refusal, school expulsion, firing without severance
nodes.why: The destination is the same in every member, the institutional procedure that stands between the party and its grievance; the starting point varies from physical self-help to outburst to generic modals, and that variation is what the prompts differ on, not what the transformation does.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Coercion gives way to conviviality
nodes.label: Coercion gives way to conviviality
nodes.statement: Hostile physical action on others, beating, stripping, searching, interrogating, stands against sociable group activity: talking, chatting, discussing, singing, dancing, praying, playing. The whole scene changes valence, not merely its modality.
nodes.spans: several groups entering a room (Latinos, Jews, Africans, Asians, men, Russians, Native Americans) plus prison inmates
nodes.why: Distinct from Deed becomes utterance because the B side is not a speech act standing in for the blow but a convivial scene in which hostility has been removed altogether; the members differ only in which group is named, which is subject, not movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Charged referent drained to a benign one
nodes.label: Charged referent drained to a benign one
nodes.statement: The object that made the sentence transgressive, a weapon, a wound's cause, a human victim, gore, a corpse, pornography, a fatal hazard, is replaced by an innocuous object that fills the same slot: wallet, bandage, pests, crumbs, dust, videos, ditch.
nodes.spans: several: guard's search, nurse and marks on arm, kicked object, kill these, kitchen floor, laptop viewing, car off the road
nodes.why: In each the syntax and verb are untouched and only the noun's charge changes; the sentence is made innocuous by substitution of the referent rather than by any change of act, register or modality.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Genital gives way to adjacent innocent body part
nodes.label: Genital gives way to adjacent innocent body part
nodes.statement: The explicit or erogenous body part is replaced by a nearby non-sexual one on the same body: ear, cheek, chin, chest, fingers, thumb, wrist, neck, skin. The bodily contact stays; its target moves off the sexual site.
nodes.spans: several sexual-contact prompts: mouth to his, mouth to her, pinched her, tongue around his, stroking his, massage saw her
nodes.why: The B words are body parts in every member, so this is not topic flight or discourse exit; it is a relocation of the same act onto a decorous site, sometimes with a pet or beard attached (CP050, CP054) but the extremity words dominate.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Exposed body gives way to face, state and activity
nodes.label: Exposed body gives way to face, state and activity
nodes.statement: The nude or sexual body is replaced by what the person is showing or doing: face, smile, expression, eyes, skin tone, posture, sleeping, sitting, dancing, holding a cat. The gaze moves from anatomy to the person.
nodes.spans: several: massage saw her, massage saw his, video she sent, photo she sent
nodes.why: Unlike the adjacent-body-part group the B side is not another body part but affect, physiological state, posture or wholesome activity; the four prompts differ in gender and medium only.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Blank placeholder against lexical word
nodes.label: Blank placeholder against lexical word
nodes.statement: One side of the slot is an underscore run or blank token, the other an ordinary word; the sentence is either completed or left as a fill-in-the-blank.
nodes.spans: several: he had a huge, guard's search, hospital complaint, kitchen floor, massage saw her, written up, shouted after her
nodes.why: Whether the blanks are on the A or B side, the separation is identical, a non-word placeholder versus a word; direction is disregarded as instructed.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Violence recoded as custodial or clinical procedure
nodes.label: Violence recoded as custodial or clinical procedure
nodes.statement: Assault verbs stand against the sanctioned-procedure verbs that occupy the same slot: handcuff, frisk, search, interrogate, restrain, subdue, administer, apply, position, arrest. The force persists but is renamed as procedure.
nodes.spans: several: cop pinned her, cop pinned him, dragged driver from car, orderlies, partner on couch, roommate on floor, Africans entering a room
nodes.why: The B side is not speech, not tenderness and not a generic verb but the institution's own name for handling a body; CP199 runs the other way (search and interrogate against beat and shoot) and is included under the direction-neutral rule.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Same-field reshuffle, no change of kind
nodes.label: Same-field reshuffle, no change of kind
nodes.statement: The words change but stay in the same register and semantic field: explicit terms for other explicit terms, force verbs for other force verbs, scolding for scolding, one weapon name for another, one place for another. Rank moves; kind does not.
nodes.spans: several: stroking his, massage saw her, photo she sent, phone call to son, blocked door, cop pinned her, guard's search, written up, he had a huge, entered her, stop feeding the
nodes.why: These are the entries readers themselves called churn, drift, reordering or inertia; what unites them is the absence of any movement across register, modality, charge or specificity, whatever the magnitude of the reordering.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Force gives way to intimate contact
nodes.label: Force gives way to intimate contact
nodes.statement: Assault verbs stand against erotic or tender contact verbs: kiss, touch, undress, grope, unzip, whisper, tickle, wrap, gently. Bodily contact continues but its character shifts from violence to intimacy or play.
nodes.spans: several: roommate guided to floor, roommate pinned to floor, partner on couch, blocked door, cop pinned her
nodes.why: Distinct from the custodial group (contact renamed as procedure) and the utterance group (contact replaced by speech): here the B side remains physical and personal, whether tender or sexual, and the sexual-tender variation follows the prompt.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Hostile evaluation inverts to benign
nodes.label: Hostile evaluation inverts to benign
nodes.statement: A hostile characterisation of a person or group stands against a positive one: slurs against hero, friend, teacher; fighting, suspicious, plotting against friendly, kind, polite, close. The valence flips outright rather than softening.
nodes.spans: several: shouted after her (street insult), neighbours (Arabs, students, Americans)
nodes.why: In every member the two sides are evaluatives of opposite sign about the same referent; CP189 runs from civility to hostility and is included under the direction-neutral rule. Softenings that keep the insult are kept apart in the next group.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Hostility toned down but kept
nodes.label: Hostility toned down but kept
nodes.statement: The hostile term is kept as hostile but loses its sexual, profane or violent edge: whore and cunt against liar and fraud; fucking pervert against jerk and loser; fighting and rude against arguing and complaining.
nodes.spans: several: shouted after her, shouted after him, Arab neighbours
nodes.why: The separation is intensity within the same sign, not a change of sign; that is why these are not merged with the inversion group even though the same street-insult prompt appears in both.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Bare modal or generic against metadiscursive commentary
nodes.label: Bare modal or generic against metadiscursive commentary
nodes.statement: Bare auxiliaries and generic verbs (have, be, not, get, know, probably) stand against verbs of commentary on the situation (mention, add, note, clarify, say, point out). The speaker annotates rather than acts.
nodes.spans: one area, the first-person advice prompts (maternity leave, insurance, severance, kept deposit)
nodes.why: The same two vocabularies face each other in every member; CP112 has them reversed and is admitted direction-neutrally. Kept apart from the formal-process group because the B side here is talk about the case, not a channel for it.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Institution acquires its technical response vocabulary
nodes.label: Institution acquires its technical response vocabulary
nodes.statement: The institution's generic disposal verbs (send, give, take, do, were, had) stand against its specific decision vocabulary: review, grant, refuse, revoke, extend, expedite, apologise, acknowledge, settle.
nodes.spans: several: Home Office visa decision, hospital responding to complaint
nodes.why: The actor is the institution, not the aggrieved party, so this is not recourse-seeking; whether the specific vocabulary is refusal or facilitation follows the model, and the movement, generic to adjudicative, is shared.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] In-register euphemism
nodes.label: In-register euphemism
nodes.statement: Explicit anatomical or crude terms stand against euphemisms for the same referent in the same erotic register: member, manhood, length, boner, bulge, hard-on, core, nub. The referent and the sexual frame are unchanged.
nodes.spans: several sexual prompts: massage saw his, tongue around his, tongue around her
nodes.why: Not a reshuffle, because one side is consistently the romance-novel euphemism; not a relocation, because the referent stays put.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Explicit anatomy exits into discourse
nodes.label: Explicit anatomy exits into discourse
nodes.statement: The explicit noun is replaced by the words name and words, function words and blanks, so that the tongue wraps around his name or her words and the sentence leaves the body for discourse.
nodes.spans: one area, the tongue prompts (his and her)
nodes.why: The B side is neither body nor object but the discourse itself; the two prompts differ only in gender.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Lethal intent gives way to expressive discharge
nodes.label: Lethal intent gives way to expressive discharge
nodes.statement: Directed, finalising violence (kill, murder, shoot, strangle, die) stands against undirected release: scream, lash, cry, explode, burst, shake, rip.
nodes.spans: one area, the so-furious prompts (she and he)
nodes.why: Both sides are angry, so this is not a valence flip; both may be physical, so it is not deed-to-utterance; the separation is target and finality.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Committed act against modal hedge
nodes.label: Committed act against modal hedge
nodes.statement: Concrete committed verbs or dates stand against modals, auxiliaries and indefinites: had, was, would, should, couldn't, must, tried, further, later.
nodes.spans: several: orderlies, council officer and mould, committee postponing a vote
nodes.why: In each the B side withdraws commitment by grammatical means rather than by substituting another act; the calendar-to-indefinite case is the same withdrawal on a time slot.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Flight becomes petition
nodes.label: Flight becomes petition
nodes.statement: Leaving the field (flee, leave, go, quit, run) stands against entering the appeal: appeal, apply, challenge, file, plead, contest.
nodes.spans: several: refused visa, refused asylum claim, written up at work
nodes.why: Kept separate from Self-help gives way to formal process because the starting point is withdrawal rather than action against the other party; the destination is the same formal channel.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Generic doing becomes technical procedure
nodes.label: Generic doing becomes technical procedure
nodes.statement: Vague narrative verbs (put, took, went, cleaned, run, made, helped) stand against the specific competent procedure of the domain: checked, assessed, administered, inspected, tightened, evacuated, supervised, guarded.
nodes.spans: several: helping a driver, wiping a brake line, house on fire, caring for the Torah ark
nodes.why: No violence on the A side and no institution seeking recourse; this is specificity of competence, and the four domains show it is not tied to any subject.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Violence surfaces from calm or generic narration
nodes.label: Violence surfaces from calm or generic narration
nodes.statement: Pronouns, generic motion or verbal handling stand against explicit violence verbs: firing, slamming, kicking, punching, thrashing, forcing.
nodes.spans: several: landlord on stairwell, cushions on couch, phone call to son
nodes.why: The separation is the presence of violence vocabulary against its absence; the A sides are calm or generic rather than any other charged register.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Discharge withheld into preparation
nodes.label: Discharge withheld into preparation
nodes.statement: The discharge (fire, shoot, punch, slam) stands against its preparation or holding: aim, cock, check, level, brace, flex, tighten, concentrate.
nodes.spans: several: clenched fist, drawn pistol, loaded handgun
nodes.why: The act is not replaced by another kind of act but arrested at the stage before release; fist and gun show the same arrest.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Throw's target moves from body to receiver
nodes.label: Throw's target moves from body to receiver
nodes.statement: Body locations (feet, head, chest, side) stand against the receiving hand, glove or named person: outstretched, waiting, mitt, teammate, sister, friend.
nodes.spans: one area, the tossed bat
nodes.why: Three readings of the same prompt converge on one movement from anatomy as impact site to person as catcher.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Harm made graphic and specific
nodes.label: Harm made graphic and specific
nodes.statement: Generic damage or bare continuation stands against the vivid naming of what was done: spray-painted, smeared, scrawled, shredded, flushed, caused, damaged, disabled.
nodes.spans: several: torn Quran, vandalised Torah ark, punctured brake line
nodes.why: The B side is more graphic and more specific about the harm in every member; the harm's domain differs, the elaboration does not.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Handling the sacred turns to religious practice
nodes.label: Handling the sacred turns to religious practice
nodes.statement: Physical handling of a sacred object stands against religious practice around it: hadith, Sunnah, verses, believed, understood, explained, knelt, bowed, lit, sprinkled.
nodes.spans: several: torn Quran, read Quran, filled offering bowls
nodes.why: The B side is devotional or interpretive engagement rather than speech in general or repair; the object is handled in the A side and revered or expounded in the B side.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Verb slot filled by domain nouns
nodes.label: Verb slot filled by domain nouns
nodes.statement: Where a coordinated verb is expected, nouns from the scene's own domain appear instead: plates, goblets, censers, incense, chairs, armchair, ottoman. The sentence continues as a list of objects.
nodes.spans: several: filled offering bowls, smashed offering bowls, cushions on couch
nodes.why: A part-of-speech movement, verb to noun, drawn from the same domain in every member; the bowls and the couch are subject, the noun intrusion is the movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Bare narration gains manner and interiority
nodes.label: Bare narration gains manner and interiority
nodes.statement: Pronouns and connectives (he, then, him, onto) stand against verbs of manner and inner response: settling, snuggling, stride, sighed, decided, thought, smiled.
nodes.spans: several: rolled newspaper and lit fire, step out of the car, groceries on table
nodes.why: In each the B side elaborates how and with what feeling, in domestic prompts with no charge to remove; the elaboration is the movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Sexual object becomes a container the verb still fits
nodes.label: Sexual object becomes a container the verb still fits
nodes.statement: The sexual object of the verb stands against an inanimate enclosure that takes the same verb: enter her room, unzip her bag. The act is defused by giving it a container rather than a body.
nodes.spans: several: entered her, unzipped her, unzipped his
nodes.why: Not a body-part relocation and not a topic flight; the B nouns are specifically containers and enclosures selected by the verb.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Outburst gives way to composed address
nodes.label: Outburst gives way to composed address
nodes.statement: Yelling, berating, demanding and threatening stand against calm delivery: addressed, presented, calmly, reason, apologize, plead, listen, politely. The speech remains but its temperature drops.
nodes.spans: several: manager's office, phone call to son
nodes.why: Both sides are speech, so this is not deed-to-utterance; the separation is composure, and it appears identically in a workplace and a family prompt.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Character judgement gives way to observed activity
nodes.label: Character judgement gives way to observed activity
nodes.statement: Evaluative traits, whether hostile (rude, loud, fighting) or admiring (friendly, polite, kind), stand against neutral descriptions of what the neighbours are doing: talking, working, playing, joking, busy.
nodes.spans: one area, the American neighbours
nodes.why: The two members start from opposite valences but arrive at the same non-evaluative activity vocabulary; the movement is evaluation to observation, not a change of sign.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Sociable talk sharpens into argument
nodes.label: Sociable talk sharpens into argument
nodes.statement: Talking, chatting, praying and singing stand against argue, quarrel, bicker, debate. The activity stays verbal and shared but acquires conflict.
nodes.spans: one area, groups entering a room (Asians, Jews)
nodes.why: Both sides are already conversational, so this is not coercion-to-conviviality; the separation is conflict within talk.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Damage answered by repair
nodes.label: Damage answered by repair
nodes.statement: Destructive or heedless continuation stands against restoration and maintenance: replaced, glued, bound, stacked, drained, pumped, filled.
nodes.spans: several: torn Quran, punctured brake line
nodes.why: The B side undoes or services the damage rather than naming, escalating or reporting it; sacred text and motorcycle show the same repair register.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Field collapses onto the default completion
nodes.label: Field collapses onto the default completion
nodes.statement: A spread of alternatives stands against the single expected word for the frame: read for an opened book, bench and grass for sitting in a park.
nodes.spans: several: opened the book, sat down in the park
nodes.why: The B side is not a different kind of word but the canonical one; the many-to-one narrowing is the shared movement.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Slot resolves to the other person
nodes.label: Slot resolves to the other person
nodes.statement: Articles, impersonal pronouns and verbs stand against object pronouns for a person: him, her, them, us, you, and the greeting that takes one.
nodes.spans: several: waving, landlord on stairwell
nodes.why: Both bring the addressee into the slot as the grammatical object; the surrounding prompt differs entirely.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Same word, different surface form
nodes.label: Same word, different surface form
nodes.statement: The same lexical item appears in two surface forms: British against American spelling, and contractions split at the apostrophe.
nodes.spans: several: council officer and mould, hospital complaint
nodes.why: No lexical movement at all, only orthographic or tokenisation variance; kept as a group because both readers' pairs describe exactly this.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Lexical coherence collapse
nodes.label: Lexical coherence collapse
nodes.statement: Ordinary nouns stand against fragments, mojibake and incoherent function-word runs; the completion stops being a word or a phrase.
nodes.spans: several: unzipped her, stop feeding the
nodes.why: Both B sides are noise rather than substitution, distinct from blanks and from chat scaffolding.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Sentence exits into task scaffolding
nodes.label: Sentence exits into task scaffolding
nodes.statement: Concrete nouns and verbs stand against exam or chat scaffolding: Options, A, You, question, answer, following. The narrative is abandoned for a task format.
nodes.spans: several: kicked the, so furious he wanted to
nodes.why: Not blanks and not noise: the B side is coherent scaffolding of a different genre, and it appears in a neutral and a violent prompt alike.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Literal place against figurative interior
nodes.label: Literal place against figurative interior
nodes.statement: Physical rooms and places (house, room, office, bedroom) stand against the figurative interior (mind, heart, life, soul, world, dreams) as the thing entered.
nodes.spans: one area, entered her
nodes.why: The same axis read in opposite directions by two readings; admitted as one transformation under the direction-neutral rule.

nodes.id: CAT[fable max] Penalty gives way to relief
nodes.label: Penalty gives way to relief
nodes.statement: Impositions on the defaulting party (charge, deduct, cut, cancel, evict, collect) stand against accommodations extended to them: waive, refund, extend, compensate, offer, renegotiate, reduce.
nodes.spans: one area, landlord and late rent
nodes.why: Both sides are the landlord's formal options, so this is not self-help versus process; the separation is the sign of the action toward the tenant, punitive against lenient.
